## 48/96 vs 24/48 Schedule: Hours, Days Off and Which Is Better
URL: https://crewdays.app/48-96-vs-24-48/

Home / 48/96 vs 24/48
48/96 vs 24/48 schedule
Same hours (about 56 a week, 2,920 a year) and the same three platoons. The 48/96 joins two shifts into a 48-hour stretch and gives four days off in a row, so there are half as many commutes. The 24/48 keeps each stretch at 24 hours, which many find easier to recover from.
Side by side
| | Point | 48/96 | 24/48
| Shift length | 24 h | 24 h
| Cycle | 6 days | 3 days
| Crews for 24/7 | 3 | 3
| Shifts a year | 121.7 | 121.7
| Hours a week | 56 | 56
| Hours a year | 2,920 | 2,920
| Most shifts in a row | 2 | 1
| Longest break | 4 days | 2 days
| Full weekends off in 2027* | 25 | 18
*For one crew, with the cycle starting on Monday, January 4, 2027. Other crews and start days get a different count.
Both cycles, day by day
48/96
Crew A: 24h, 24h, Off, Off, Off, Off
Crew B: Off, Off, Off, Off, 24h, 24h
Crew C: Off, Off, 24h, 24h, Off, Off
24/48
Crew A: 24h, Off, Off
Crew B: Off, Off, 24h
Crew C: Off, 24h, Off
48/96 Schedule calendar 24/48 Schedule calendar
Which one suits you
Both use three platoons and the same 56-hour average week, and both put 9 or 10 shifts into any 28-day 7(k) work period, so overtime and pay are about the same.
The 48/96 halves the trips to the station: about 61 commutes a year instead of about 122. That matters most for firefighters who live an hour or more away. You also get four days off in a row every six days.
The 24/48 keeps each stretch at 24 hours, so a bad night is followed by two days off rather than another 24 hours on duty. Swaps are easier too, because a colleague covers one shift, not two.
How to choose
Put both patterns side by side in the calendar with your own start date: weekends off, holidays worked and pay depend on where your crew sits in the cycle, not only on the pattern. Then compare yearly pay at your hourly rate in the shift pay calculator, which applies federal and state overtime.
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate

Is the 48/96 or the 24/48 schedule better?
Same hours (about 56 a week, 2,920 a year) and the same three platoons. The 48/96 joins two shifts into a 48-hour stretch and gives four days off in a row, so there are half as many commutes. The 24/48 keeps each stretch at 24 hours, which many find easier to recover from.
Which has more days off, 48/96 or 24/48?
4 days off every 6 days on the 48/96 and 2 every 3 on the 24/48. Hours a week: 56 and 56.

## Pay Period Calendar 2027: Biweekly, 26 or 27 Paydays? (Free)
URL: https://crewdays.app/pay-period-calendar-2027/

Home / Pay period calendar 2027
Pay period calendar 2027
Enter any payday you know. You get every payday of the year, the months with three biweekly paychecks (or five weekly ones) and whether it is a 27-paycheck year.
| | Month | Count | Dates
| January | 2 | Fri, Jan 8, Fri, Jan 22
| February | 2 | Fri, Feb 5, Fri, Feb 19
| March | 2 | Fri, Mar 5, Fri, Mar 19
| April | 3 | Fri, Apr 2, Fri, Apr 16, Fri, Apr 30
| May | 2 | Fri, May 14, Fri, May 28
| June | 2 | Fri, Jun 11, Fri, Jun 25
| July | 2 | Fri, Jul 9, Fri, Jul 23
| August | 2 | Fri, Aug 6, Fri, Aug 20
| September | 2 | Fri, Sep 3, Fri, Sep 17
| October | 3 | Fri, Oct 1, Fri, Oct 15, Fri, Oct 29
| November | 2 | Fri, Nov 12, Fri, Nov 26
| December | 2 | Fri, Dec 10, Fri, Dec 24
Is 2027 a 27-paycheck year?
A year has 52 weeks and one day (two in a leap year), so the paydays slowly move earlier. Every 11 years or so a biweekly payroll fits 27 paydays into one year instead of 26, and a weekly payroll fits 53 instead of 52. 2027 starts on a Friday and is not a leap year, so it has 53 Fridays.
Paid every Friday: 53 paydays in 2027.
Paid every other Friday: 27 paydays only if the first one is Friday, January 1, 2027. That day is New Year's Day, so many employers pay on Thursday, December 31, 2026 instead, and 2027 then has 26 (26 if your first payday is January 8, 27 if it is January 15).
| | Year | Weekly: 53 paydays if paid on | Biweekly: 27 paydays if the first payday is
| 2026 | Thursday | Thursday, January 1
| 2027 | Friday | Friday, January 1
| 2028 | Saturday and Sunday | Saturday, January 1; Sunday, January 2
Calculated from the calendar. Your employer may move a payday that falls on a holiday or weekend, which can move a paycheck into the year before.
Months with three paychecks in 2027
| | First Friday payday | Paydays | Three-paycheck months
| January 1 | 27 | January, July, December
| January 8 | 26 | April, October
| January 15 | 27 | January, July, December
Paid biweekly on another weekday? Put one of your paydays in the calculator above.
Federal pay periods 2027
Federal employees are paid every two weeks on a Sunday-to-Saturday cycle. The leave year begins with the first day of the first complete pay period of the calendar year (5 CFR 630.201), so the 2027 leave year runs from Sunday, January 10, 2027 to Saturday, January 8, 2028: 26 pay periods.
| | Pay period | Starts | Ends
| 1 | Sun, Jan 10, 2027 | Sat, Jan 23, 2027
| 2 | Sun, Jan 24, 2027 | Sat, Feb 6, 2027
| 3 | Sun, Feb 7, 2027 | Sat, Feb 20, 2027
| 4 | Sun, Feb 21, 2027 | Sat, Mar 6, 2027
| 5 | Sun, Mar 7, 2027 | Sat, Mar 20, 2027
| 6 | Sun, Mar 21, 2027 | Sat, Apr 3, 2027
| 7 | Sun, Apr 4, 2027 | Sat, Apr 17, 2027
| 8 | Sun, Apr 18, 2027 | Sat, May 1, 2027
| 9 | Sun, May 2, 2027 | Sat, May 15, 2027
| 10 | Sun, May 16, 2027 | Sat, May 29, 2027
| 11 | Sun, May 30, 2027 | Sat, Jun 12, 2027
| 12 | Sun, Jun 13, 2027 | Sat, Jun 26, 2027
| 13 | Sun, Jun 27, 2027 | Sat, Jul 10, 2027
| 14 | Sun, Jul 11, 2027 | Sat, Jul 24, 2027
| 15 | Sun, Jul 25, 2027 | Sat, Aug 7, 2027
| 16 | Sun, Aug 8, 2027 | Sat, Aug 21, 2027
| 17 | Sun, Aug 22, 2027 | Sat, Sep 4, 2027
| 18 | Sun, Sep 5, 2027 | Sat, Sep 18, 2027
| 19 | Sun, Sep 19, 2027 | Sat, Oct 2, 2027
| 20 | Sun, Oct 3, 2027 | Sat, Oct 16, 2027
| 21 | Sun, Oct 17, 2027 | Sat, Oct 30, 2027
| 22 | Sun, Oct 31, 2027 | Sat, Nov 13, 2027
| 23 | Sun, Nov 14, 2027 | Sat, Nov 27, 2027
| 24 | Sun, Nov 28, 2027 | Sat, Dec 11, 2027
| 25 | Sun, Dec 12, 2027 | Sat, Dec 25, 2027
| 26 | Sun, Dec 26, 2027 | Sat, Jan 8, 2028
Payday comes a few days after each period ends and depends on your payroll provider (NFC, DFAS, DOI IBC or GSA), so check your agency's calendar for the exact date. Annual leave above the carryover limit (usually 240 hours, 5 U.S.C. 6304) is forfeited at the end of the leave year, so the last day to use 2027 leave is Saturday, January 8, 2028.
What a 27th paycheck means
If you are paid by the hour, a 27th payday is one more paycheck for two more weeks of work. If you are on a yearly salary, check how your employer divides it: some divide the salary by 27 that year, so each paycheck is a little smaller; others keep 26 equal paychecks and pay the extra one on top. Deductions taken per paycheck, such as health premiums or retirement contributions, may also come out 27 times.
Shift workers paid every two weeks can see their paydays next to their shifts: enter “A payday” under “Your pay” in the shift calendar. The shift pay calculator works out yearly pay by pattern.
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
How many pay periods are in 2027?
26 for most biweekly payrolls and 52 for weekly ones. You get 27 biweekly paydays only if the first is Friday, January 1, 2027, and 53 weekly paydays if you are paid on Fridays.
How many Fridays are in 2027?
53. 2027 starts and ends on a Friday.
Which months have three paychecks in 2027?
With Friday paydays starting January 8: April and October. Starting January 15: January and July and December.
When does the 2027 federal leave year start?
On Sunday, January 10, 2027, the first day of the first complete pay period of 2027 (5 CFR 630.201). It ends on Saturday, January 8, 2028, after 26 pay periods.
Is 2026 a 27-paycheck year?
On the calendar, only for biweekly payrolls whose first payday of 2026 was Thursday, January 1. Payrolls paid every other Friday from January 2 can also reach 27 if the employer moves the January 1, 2027 payday (New Year's Day) back to Thursday, December 31, 2026. Weekly payrolls paid on Thursday get 53 paydays in 2026.

## 9/80 Schedule Explained: 2027 Calendar, Every Other Friday Off
URL: https://crewdays.app/9-80-schedule/

Home / 9/80 schedule
9/80 schedule calendar
On a 9/80 schedule you work 80 hours in nine days: eight 9-hour days and one 8-hour day, with every other Friday off. Enter your first Friday off and get all of them for the year.
| | Month | Count | Dates
| January | 2 | Fri, Jan 8, Fri, Jan 22
| February | 2 | Fri, Feb 5, Fri, Feb 19
| March | 2 | Fri, Mar 5, Fri, Mar 19
| April | 3 | Fri, Apr 2, Fri, Apr 16, Fri, Apr 30
| May | 2 | Fri, May 14, Fri, May 28
| June | 2 | Fri, Jun 11, Fri, Jun 25
| July | 2 | Fri, Jul 9, Fri, Jul 23
| August | 2 | Fri, Aug 6, Fri, Aug 20
| September | 2 | Fri, Sep 3, Fri, Sep 17
| October | 3 | Fri, Oct 1, Fri, Oct 15, Fri, Oct 29
| November | 2 | Fri, Nov 12, Fri, Nov 26
| December | 2 | Fri, Dec 10, Fri, Dec 24
How a 9/80 schedule works
| | Week | Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Total
| Week 1 | 9 | 9 | 9 | 9 | 8 | 44
| Week 2 | 9 | 9 | 9 | 9 | off | 36
That is 80 hours every two weeks, the same as five 8-hour days, with 26 extra days off a year (27 in a year with 53 Fridays, such as 2027, depending on where your cycle falls).
Overtime: why the Friday is split
Under the Fair Labor Standards Act overtime is due for hours over 40 in a workweek, and the workweek is “a fixed and regularly recurring period of 168 hours” that “may begin on any day and at any hour of the day” (29 CFR 778.105). Week 1 above has 44 hours, so with a normal Monday-to-Sunday workweek the 4 extra hours would be overtime.
Employers avoid this by starting the workweek in the middle of the 8-hour Friday, for example at noon. Four of the Friday hours then belong to week 1 and four to week 2, and each workweek has exactly 40 hours. The start time must stay fixed; it can only be changed permanently and not to avoid overtime.
California is different: overtime is also due after 8 hours in a day unless a valid alternative workweek schedule was adopted by a secret-ballot vote (California Labor Code 511). Without one, the ninth hour of each day is overtime there.
Holidays on a 9/80
A holiday on a 9-hour day is a 9-hour day off, but many employers pay 8 hours of holiday pay, so you use one hour of leave or make it up. When a holiday falls on your Friday off, some employers give another day off and some do not. The calculator lists the federal holidays (on their actual date) that fall on your Fridays off; check your own policy.
Similar schedules
The 4/10 (four 10-hour days a week) and the 5/4/9 (a 9/80 by another name) are also compressed workweeks. For rotating shifts that cover nights and weekends, see the shift calendar.
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
How many Fridays off do you get on a 9/80 in 2027?
26 or 27. 2027 has 53 Fridays, so if your first Friday off is January 1 you get 27, otherwise 26.
Is a 9/80 schedule legal?
Yes. Federal law only requires overtime after 40 hours in a workweek, and the 9/80 keeps each workweek at 40 hours by starting it in the middle of the 8-hour Friday (29 CFR 778.105). Some states with daily overtime, such as California, need an approved alternative workweek.
What is the difference between a 9/80 and a 4/10?
A 9/80 gives one Friday off every two weeks with 9-hour days; a 4/10 gives a day off every week with 10-hour days.
Is a 9/80 schedule worth it?
Yes, if a three-day weekend every other week is worth one extra hour on eight days of every fortnight: you get 26 a year (27 in some years) with no change in pay. It only avoids overtime if the workweek is split on the short Friday, as explained above, and it suits less well if you must be home at a fixed time every evening.

## 12 Hour Shift Schedule Examples: Weekends Off, 7 Days Off
URL: https://crewdays.app/12-hour-shift-schedules/

Home / 12-hour shift schedules
12-hour shift schedule examples
With 12-hour shifts, four crews cover every hour of the year: two on days and two on nights. Each person averages 42 hours a week, 2,190 a year. What changes between schedules is how the days off fall.
The common 12-hour schedules side by side
| | Schedule | Cycle | Full weekends off in 2027* | Longest break | Most shifts in a row | Nights | Federal overtime a year*
| Pitman | 14 days | 26 | 3 days | 3 | Fixed crews | 520 h
| Panama | 28 days | 26 | 3 days | 3 | Rotate | 520 h
| DuPont | 28 days | 26 | 7 days | 4 | Rotate | 624 h
| 4 on 4 off | 8 days | 21 | 4 days | 4 | Fixed crews | 208 h
| 4-3-3-4 | 14 days | 52 | 4 days | 4 | Fixed crews | 208 h
| 3 on 3 off | 6 days | 17 | 3 days | 3 | Fixed crews | 208 h
| 2 on 2 off | 4 days | 13 | 2 days | 2 | Fixed crews | 208 h
| 7 on 7 off | 14 days | 26 | 7 days | 7 | Fixed crews | 1,144 h
*One crew, cycle and workweek both starting Monday, January 4, 2027. Other crews and start days give different counts; each pattern page shows all of them. The 4-3-3-4 crew in this example never works a weekend because the two-crew version does not cover Saturdays and Sundays; half of the DuPont's 26 weekends fall inside its 7-day breaks. The overtime column uses the federal weekly rule; California and Alaska also pay daily overtime on 12-hour shifts, and Colorado on hours beyond 12 (see overtime after 8 or 12 hours).
12-hour shift schedule with every other weekend off
Pitman and Panama give a full weekend off every other week, because the cycle packs three shifts into Friday to Sunday one week and leaves Friday to Sunday free the next. On the Pitman that means a three-day weekend every two weeks.
12-hour shift schedule with 7 days off
DuPont is the common 12-hour schedule that gives a full week off: once every 28 days, after a block of four day shifts. Taking those four shifts as leave turns it into 14 days off in a row. The cost is uneven weeks, from 0 to 72 hours, and a quick change from days to nights in the middle of the cycle. The 7 on 7 off schedule gives a week off every other week instead: seven 12-hour shifts in a row, then seven days off, 84 hours every two weeks.
12-hour shift schedules for police
Common choices in police departments include Pitman, Panama, 4 on 4 off, 4-3-3-4 and 7 on 7 off. Departments that want officers to stay on days or nights use the Pitman with fixed crews; those that want everyone to share nights rotate crews every two weeks, which is the Panama. Many police agencies pay overtime under section 7(k), after 171 hours in a 28-day work period (29 CFR 553.230); check yours in the 7(k) calculator. More on police shift schedules.
How many crews does a 12-hour schedule need?
Four for 24/7 coverage: 168 hours a week divided by 4 crews is 42 hours each. Two crews can cover only day shifts (or only nights). With three crews each person would work 56 hours a week. For 8- and 24-hour options, see 24/7 shift schedule examples.
12-hour or 8-hour shifts?
12-hour shifts mean about 182 working days a year instead of about 260 with five 8-hour days, so fewer commutes and more days off, and only two handovers a day. The price is long days: fatigue in the last hours, little time for anything else on work days and, on rotating schedules, frequent changes between days and nights. Overtime also depends on the state: in California hours over 8 in a day are overtime unless an alternative workweek has been adopted (California Labor Code 510 and 511).
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
What is the best 12-hour shift schedule?
It depends on what you value. The Pitman and Panama give every other weekend off and never more than three shifts in a row; the DuPont gives a full week off every four weeks; 2 on 2 off keeps runs to two shifts. All average 42 hours a week with four crews.
Which 12-hour schedule has every other weekend off?
Pitman and Panama. A crew that starts its cycle on a Monday has Friday to Sunday off every other week.
Which 12-hour schedule gives 7 days off?
The DuPont: four nights, three off, three days, one off, three nights, three off, four days and then seven days off, a 28-day cycle.
How many hours a year is a 12-hour shift schedule?
About 2,190 scheduled hours on four-crew schedules (182.5 shifts of 12 hours), before overtime, leave and swaps.
Is a 12-hour shift overtime?
Not under federal law. Overtime is due only after 40 hours in the workweek (29 CFR 778.102 and 778.105), so three 12-hour shifts pay none and a fourth in the same week pays 8 hours. California pays after 8 hours in a day and double time after 12 (Labor Code 510), Alaska after 8 and Colorado after 12.
How many 12-hour shifts is 2,000 hours?
About 167, since 2,000 ÷ 12 = 166.7. A full-time year of 2,080 hours is about 173 twelve-hour shifts, and three 12s a week for 52 weeks is 156.

---

## 24/7 Shift Schedule Examples: Crews, Hours and Overtime
URL: https://crewdays.app/24-7-shift-schedule/

Home / 24/7 shift schedules
24/7 shift schedules compared
Covering every hour of the year takes 8,760 hours per position. How you split them decides how many crews you need, how long people work and how much overtime you pay.
How many crews for 24/7?
A week has 168 hours. Divide them by the number of crews to get the average week of each person, whatever the shift length:
| | Crews per position | Average hours a week | Hours a year | Typical schedules
| 3 | 56 | 2,920 | 24-hour shifts: 24/48, 48/96, Kelly. Outside fire departments, which use the 7(k) exemption, that is about 16 hours of weekly overtime per person.
| 4 | 42 | 2,190 | 12-hour patterns (Pitman, DuPont, Panama, 4 on 4 off…), the 8-hour southern swing and the 24/72.
| 5 | 33.6 | 1,752 | Five-crew schedules, usually 8-hour shifts, often with the spare time used for training, relief and leave cover.
40 hours a week would need 4.2 crews, so most 24/7 operations run four crews at 42 hours and pay about 2 hours of overtime a week on average (more when the weeks are uneven), or add relief staff.
The schedules side by side
| | Schedule | Shift | Crews | Hours a week | Days and nights | Most shifts in a row | Longest break | Overtime hours a year*
| Pitman, crews fixed on days or nights | 12 h | 4 | 42 | Fixed | 3 | 3 days | 520
| Panama (rotating 2-2-3) | 12 h | 4 | 42 | Rotate | 3 | 3 days | 520
| DuPont | 12 h | 4 | 42 | Rotate | 4 | 7 days | 624
| 4 on 4 off, rotating | 12 h | 4 | 42 | Rotate | 4 | 4 days | 208
| 3 on 3 off, rotating | 12 h | 4 | 42 | Rotate | 3 | 3 days | 208
| 2 on 2 off, rotating | 12 h | 4 | 42 | Rotate | 2 | 2 days | 208
| Continental (2 days, 2 nights, 4 off) | 12 h | 4 | 42 | Rotate | 4 | 4 days | 208
| 14/14 hitch, day and night crews | 12 h | 4 | 42 | Fixed | 14 | 14 days | 1,144
| Southern swing (8-hour days, evenings, nights) | 8 h | 4 | 42 | Rotate | 7 | 3 days | 208
| 24/48 | 24 h | 3 | 56 | Whole day | 1 | 2 days | 7(k)
| 48/96 | 24 h | 3 | 56 | Whole day | 2 | 4 days | 7(k)
| Kelly | 24 h | 3 | 56 | Whole day | 1 | 4 days | 7(k)
| 24/72 | 24 h | 4 | 42 | Whole day | 1 | 3 days | 7(k)
*Per person, federal rule (over 40 hours in a workweek), crew A with the cycle and the workweek both starting on Monday. Moving the start of the workweek changes it; each pattern page shows all seven options. 24-hour fire schedules use 7(k) work periods instead (29 CFR 553.230).
How to choose
Start with shift length. 12-hour shifts need only two handovers a day and give people about half the days of the year off, but some jobs and some people cannot sustain 12 hours. 8-hour shifts mean three handovers and more days at work, but shorter days.
Then decide on nights. Fixed crews (a Pitman with day and night crews) let people stay on one shift, which suits those who prefer nights; rotating patterns share nights fairly but make everyone change their sleep. If you rotate, faster rotations (2 or 3 nights at a time) and forward rotation (days, then evenings, then nights) are often preferred because they change the body clock less.
Finally, look at the weeks as well as the average. A DuPont and a Pitman both average 42 hours, but the DuPont has weeks of 72 hours and weeks of none, which costs more in weekly overtime unless the workweek is set carefully. Put the candidates in the shift calendar with “All crews” to see coverage day by day, and compare pay in the shift pay calculator.
Headcount
Four crews cover one position, but leave and sickness still have to be covered. Each person on a 42-hour rota is entitled to the leave in their contract (in the UK at least 5.6 weeks a year under the Working Time Regulations), so plan relief or overtime for those weeks. In the UK, check each rota against the 48-hour average week and the 11-hour daily rest on the UK rota page, read the working time rules for shift workers and plan cover for the bank holidays.
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
How many employees do I need for 24/7 coverage?
8,760 hours a year per position. With four crews each person works about 2,190 scheduled hours (42 a week), so you need four people per position before leave and sickness. With three crews on 24-hour shifts each works 2,920 hours.
What is the best shift schedule for 24/7 coverage?
There is no single best one. For 12-hour shifts the Pitman gives every other weekend off and can keep crews on fixed days or nights; the DuPont gives a full week off every four weeks; 2 on 2 off keeps runs short. Fire departments mostly use the 24/48 with three platoons.
Can you cover 24/7 with three crews on 8-hour shifts?
Only if each crew works every day, about 56 hours a week with no days off, which breaks rest rules in many places and causes heavy overtime. Four or five crews are the usual minimum for 8-hour shifts.

---

## Daylight Saving Night Shift: Hours and Pay (2026–2028)
URL: https://crewdays.app/daylight-saving-night-shift/

Home / Daylight saving time
Night shift on the night the clocks change
In the US, clocks go back one hour on the first Sunday of November and forward on the second Sunday of March, both at 2:00 a.m. A 12-hour night shift then lasts 13 hours in the fall and 11 in the spring.
How the extra or missing hour is paid
Under the Fair Labor Standards Act you are paid for the hours you actually work (29 CFR Part 785). In the fall, an hourly worker on nights works one hour more than the schedule shows, and that hour counts towards overtime for the week. In the spring the shift is one hour shorter. Salaried and exempt staff are usually paid the same either way. Union contracts and state laws can give more, so check yours.
Arizona (except the Navajo Nation), Hawaii and the US territories do not change their clocks.
Calendar files from Crewdays use all-day events, so your shifts do not move in your phone calendar when the clocks change.
Clock change dates 2026 to 2028
| | Year | US: forward (spring) | US: back (fall) | UK: forward | UK: back
| 2026 | March 8 | November 1 | March 29 | October 25
| 2027 | March 14 | November 7 | March 28 | October 31
| 2028 | March 12 | November 5 | March 26 | October 29
US: at 2:00 a.m. local time (15 U.S.C. 260a). UK: forward at 1:00 a.m. on the last Sunday in March and back at 2:00 a.m. on the last Sunday in October (GOV.UK).
How long common shifts last that night
| | Shift | Normal | Clocks go back | Clocks go forward
| 12-hour night, 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. | 12 h | 13 h | 11 h
| 8-hour night, 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. | 8 h | 9 h | 7 h
| 24-hour shift, 7 a.m. to 7 a.m. | 24 h | 25 h | 23 h
| 48-hour shift starting Saturday | 48 h | 49 h | 47 h
| Day shift, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Sunday | 12 h | 12 h | 12 h
Only shifts that are running at 2:00 a.m. on the Sunday change length. A shift that starts after the change, for example 3:00 a.m., is normal.
Firefighters and police on 24-hour shifts
Under section 7(k) the extra hour in the fall counts towards the hours of the work period, so on a 28-day period it brings firefighters one hour closer to the 212-hour overtime threshold (29 CFR 553.230). Check it in the 7(k) overtime calculator. Police have the same rule with a 171-hour threshold.
Getting through the night
In the fall the last hour of a night shift is the hardest: you are an hour further from your last sleep. Plan breaks for the end of the shift and arrange a lift home if you can. In the spring you lose an hour of sleep before a day shift on Sunday, so go to bed earlier on Saturday. Phones and computers change time on their own, but the clocks of time-clock terminals and older equipment may not.
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
When do the clocks change?
Second Sunday of March and first Sunday of November at 2:00 a.m. local time: November 1, 2026, March 14, 2027 and November 7, 2027.
Do I get paid for the extra hour on a night shift?
If you are paid by the hour, yes: the FLSA counts hours actually worked, so a 13-hour shift is paid as 13 hours.
How does daylight saving time affect night shift workers?
Twice a year the night changes length. In November a 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. shift lasts 13 hours, and in March it lasts 11. The longer night is paid as worked and can push your week into overtime; the shorter one usually pays an hour less unless your contract guarantees the full shift.

---

## FLSA 7(k) Overtime Calculator for Firefighters and Police
URL: https://crewdays.app/flsa-7k-overtime-calculator/

Home / 7(k) overtime
FLSA 7(k) overtime calculator
Public fire and police departments can pay overtime over a work period of 7 to 28 days instead of every week. Over 28 days, firefighters get overtime after 212 hours and police officers after 171 hours.
Overtime thresholds by work period
| | Work period | Firefighters | Police
| 28 days | 212 h | 171 h
| 27 days | 204 h | 165 h
| 24 days | 182 h | 147 h
| 21 days | 159 h | 128 h
| 14 days | 106 h | 86 h
| 7 days | 53 h | 43 h
Source: 29 CFR 553.230. Departments pick their work period; it must be set in advance and stay the same. On a 24/48 schedule firefighters work about 216 to 240 hours in 28 days, so most work periods include some overtime.
How much overtime do firefighters get?
The schedule alone builds some in. On a 24/48 with a 28-day work period, about 156 hours a year fall above the 212-hour threshold before anyone works an extra shift. Covering vacancies, holdovers and recalls come on top, and those depend on your department.
| | Schedule | Hours in a 28-day period | Overtime hours a year from the schedule
| 24/48 | 216 to 240 | about 156 (148 to 172)
| 48/96 | 192 to 240 | about 199 (148 to 252)
| Kelly | 216 to 240 | about 156 (124 to 172)
| 24/72 | 168 | 0
| 24/48 with a Kelly day every 7th shift | 168 to 216 | about 12 (0 to 20)
Worked out from each cycle over 13 work periods of 28 days, for every possible start day; the range shows how the start date moves the total. A 48/96 averages the same 56 hours a week as a 24/48 but swings between 192 and 240 hours a period, so more of its hours land above the line. Kelly days exist largely to cut this built-in overtime: one every 7th shift brings a 24/48 down to about 12 hours a year.
How the regular rate is worked out
Overtime is paid at one and a half times the regular rate. The regular rate is all pay for the period, including night and shift differentials and most bonuses, divided by the hours worked (29 CFR 778.109). The calculator pays straight time for every hour plus a half-time premium for the overtime hours, which gives the same result.
Union contracts and state laws often pay more, for example overtime after fewer hours. This calculator shows the federal minimum. See also the 24/48 calendar and Kelly schedule.
Is sleep time paid on a 24-hour shift?
| | Your situation | Sleep time
| Public fire or police department on 7(k), shift of exactly 24 hours | Paid: it cannot be taken out of hours worked (29 CFR 553.222(b))
| Public fire or police department on 7(k), shift of more than 24 hours (for example 48 hours) | Up to 8 hours in each 24 can be left unpaid, but only with an agreement between the department and its employees (553.222(c))
| Private employers, including private EMS, shift of 24 hours or more | Up to 8 hours can be left unpaid with an agreement, if the employer provides beds and you can usually sleep through (29 CFR 785.22)
| Any shift under 24 hours | Paid, even if you are allowed to sleep (29 CFR 785.21)
Calls that interrupt sleep are always paid. If they leave you less than 5 hours of sleep, the whole sleep period counts as hours worked (553.222(c) and 785.22(b)).
911 dispatchers and civilian staff
The 7(k) work period is for firefighters and sworn law enforcement. Civilian employees of a police department, such as dispatchers and radio operators, are not covered by it (29 CFR 553.211(g)), so they get overtime after 40 hours in the workweek like other workers. Use the shift pay calculator with the federal rule.
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
What is the 7(k) exemption?
Section 7(k) of the FLSA lets public employers pay fire and police employees overtime over a work period of 7 to 28 days, with a higher hour threshold, instead of after 40 hours every week.
How many hours before overtime for firefighters?
212 hours in a 28-day work period, or the same proportion for shorter periods: 106 hours in 14 days, 53 in 7 days.
Do shift differentials count toward overtime pay?
Yes. Differentials and most bonuses are part of the regular rate, so they raise the overtime rate.
Do firefighters get a lot of overtime?
Some is built into the schedule. With a 28-day work period, a 24/48 puts about 156 hours a year above the 212-hour threshold and a 48/96 about 199; a 24/72 puts none. Extra shifts to cover vacancies come on top and vary by department.

How many hours a year does each shift pattern work?
| | Pattern | Hours a week (average) | Hours a year | Shifts a year
| Pitman Schedule | 42 | 2,190 | 182.5
| Panama Schedule | 42 | 2,190 | 182.5
| DuPont Schedule | 42 | 2,190 | 182.5
| 4 on 4 off Schedule | 42 | 2,190 | 182.5
| 3 on 3 off Schedule | 42 | 2,190 | 182.5
| 2 on 2 off Schedule | 42 | 2,190 | 182.5

| 24/48 Schedule | 56 | 2,920 | 121.7
| 48/96 Schedule | 56 | 2,920 | 121.7
| Kelly Schedule | 56 | 2,920 | 121.7
| 24/72 Schedule | 42 | 2,190 | 91.3
| Southern Swing Schedule | 42 | 2,190 | 273.8
| 4/10 Schedule | 40 | 2,085.7 | 208.6
| Continental Shift Pattern | 42 | 2,190 | 182.5
| 7 on 7 off Schedule | 42 | 2,190 | 182.5
| 4-5-5 Shift Pattern | 42 | 2,190 | 182.5
| 3-4-4-3 Schedule | 42 | 2,190 | 182.5
| 2 Days, 2 Nights, 2 Off (3 Crews) | 56 | 2,920 | 243.3
| 5-5-4 Schedule | 50.4 | 2,628 | 219
| 5-2-5-3 Schedule | 37.3 | 1,946.7 | 243.3
| 1-3-2-3 Schedule | 56 | 2,920 | 121.7
| Hitch Rotation Schedule | 56 | 2,920 | 243.3
Hours a year = hours in one cycle × 365 ÷ days in the cycle. The exact number in a given year changes by a few shifts depending on where your crew starts. For comparison, a regular 40-hour week is 2,080 hours a year (40 × 52 weeks), and three 12-hour shifts a week (36 hours) are 1,872.
Annual salary to hourly rate
Hourly rate = annual salary ÷ (hours a week × 52). Departments on a 56-hour week often divide by 2,912 hours (56 × 52). Your contract may use a different divisor, for example to leave out overtime built into the schedule.
Shift differential and overtime: a worked week
Night and evening differentials are part of the regular rate, so they raise your overtime pay (29 CFR 778.207(b) and 778.109). Take a week with three 12-hour nights and one 12-hour day, $25 an hour and a $3 night differential:
| Straight-time pay | 48 h × $25 + 36 night h × $3 | $1,308
| Regular rate | $1,308 ÷ 48 h | $27.25 an hour
| Overtime premium | 8 h over 40 × half of $27.25 | $109
| Total for the week | | $1,417
Working the premium out on the base rate alone ($12.50 × 8 = $100) would pay $9 too little that week. Enter your night differential above and the calculator does this for every week of the year.
What is a shift differential?
A shift differential is extra pay for working less popular hours: evenings, nights, weekends or holidays. It is usually a fixed amount for each of those hours, such as $2 more an hour on nights, or a percentage of your base rate. Federal law does not require it: the FLSA "does not require extra pay for night work" (US Department of Labor). The amount comes from your employer's policy or your union contract. Federal employees get 10% for regular night work (5 U.S.C. 5545(a)); shift hours and differentials has more benchmarks.
Does shift differential apply to overtime and PTO?
To overtime, yes: it is part of the regular rate (29 CFR 778.207(b)), as the worked week above shows. PTO is different. Vacation, holiday and sick pay are not pay for hours worked (29 CFR 778.218), so whether your PTO includes the differential depends on your employer's policy or contract.
Can a shift differential be taken away?
Usually, for shifts you have not worked yet. No federal law requires a differential, so an employer can change or end it unless a union contract or written agreement guarantees it.
Overtime after 8 or 12 hours: federal and state rules
Federal law does not require overtime for long days, only for long weeks: there is no overtime for hours over 8 in a day as such (29 CFR 778.102). It pays time and a half after 40 hours in the workweek (29 CFR 778.105), on the regular rate, which includes night differentials (29 CFR 778.109). California also pays after 8 hours in a day and double after 12 (Labor Code 510); health care employers can adopt 12-hour alternative workweeks (IWC Wage Order 5). Alaska pays after 8 hours a day (AS 23.10.060) and Colorado after 12 hours in a workday or 12 hours in a row (COMPS Order #40). Fire and police departments often use a 7(k) work period instead: see the 7(k) calculator. If you work in another state, check its labor department: a few states have their own rules, and a union contract can also pay daily overtime.
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
Which states pay overtime after 8 hours a day?
California pays time and a half after 8 hours in a workday and double time after 12 (Labor Code 510), and Alaska after 8 hours in a day (AS 23.10.060, with exemptions such as hospital employees who provide medical services). Colorado pays after 12 hours in a workday or 12 hours in a row (COMPS Order #40). Federal law only pays overtime after 40 hours in the workweek (29 CFR 778.102 and 778.105).
How much does a 12-hour Pitman schedule pay a year?
A Pitman schedule works about 2,190 hours a year, or 42 hours a week on average. At $25 an hour that is about $54,750 before overtime; with federal overtime on the weeks over 40 hours, a little more.
How many hours a year is a 48/96 schedule?
About 2,920 hours: 48 hours on and 96 off is an average of 56 hours a week.
Is overtime paid on a 24/48 schedule?
Firefighters at public departments are usually paid under the FLSA 7(k) exemption, with overtime after 212 hours in 28 days. Private employers pay overtime after 40 hours a week.

## How Many Work Hours in a Year? 2027 Has 2,088
URL: https://crewdays.app/work-hours-in-a-year/

Home / Guides / Work hours in a year
How many work hours are in a year?
Most people use 2,080: 40 hours a week times 52 weeks. 2027 has 261 weekdays, so a Monday-to-Friday job is 2,088 scheduled hours. A 12-hour rotation comes to about 2,184 hours, and a firefighter on a 24/48 works about 2,928.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @erothermel on Unsplash
Work hours by year
A year is 52 weeks and one day, or 52 weeks and two days in a leap year. Those extra days decide whether a year has 260, 261 or 262 weekdays. At 8 hours a day:
| | Year | Weekdays | Work hours | Without federal holidays (observed days off)
| 2026 | 261 | 2,088 | 250 days, 2,000 hours
| 2027 | 261 | 2,088 | 249 days, 1,992 hours
| 2028 | 260 | 2,080 | 250 days, 2,000 hours
The last column takes away the weekdays that federal employees have off for the 11 federal holidays. A holiday on a Saturday is observed on the Friday before, so New Year's Day 2028 (a Saturday) is a day off on Friday, December 31, 2027: 2027 ends up with 12 holiday weekdays and 2028 with 10. Your own employer's holiday list may be longer or shorter.
Why 2,080 hours?
2,080 is 40 hours × 52 weeks. It is a handy round number for turning an hourly wage into a salary, and most payroll and HR tools use it. A real calendar year has one or two days more than 52 weeks, so in most years a full-time weekday job has 2,088 scheduled hours, and 2,096 in a leap year that starts on a Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday. Years that start on a Saturday, such as 2028, have 260 weekdays, exactly 2,080 hours.
The federal government splits the difference. To turn an annual salary into an hourly rate it divides by 2,087, the average number of weekday hours over a long run of years (5 U.S.C. 5504(b)).
Work hours in each month of 2027
| | Month | Weekdays | Hours at 8 a day
| January | 21 | 168
| February | 20 | 160
| March | 23 | 184
| April | 22 | 176
| May | 21 | 168
| June | 22 | 176
| July | 22 | 176
| August | 22 | 176
| September | 22 | 176
| October | 21 | 168
| November | 22 | 176
| December | 23 | 184
On average a month has 173.3 work hours (2,080 ÷ 12). March and December 2027 have the most, with 23 and 23 weekdays; February has the fewest, 20.
Federal holidays in 2027
All 11 federal holidays of 2027 fall on or are observed on a weekday. Two of them move: Juneteenth (Saturday, June 19) is observed on Friday, June 18, and Christmas (Saturday, December 25) on Friday, December 24. New Year's Day 2028 is also a Saturday, so federal employees get Friday, December 31, 2027 off. That gives them 12 weekday holidays inside calendar year 2027 and 249 working days (1,992 hours). Holidays move to Friday or Monday under 5 U.S.C. 6103(b) and Executive Order 11582.
Work hours in a year on shift schedules
Rotating shifts do not follow the 5-day week, so their yearly hours come from the cycle: hours in one cycle × 365 ÷ days in the cycle. For one crew in 2027:
| | Schedule | Hours in 2027 | How
| Monday to Friday, 8 hours | 2,088 | 261 weekdays in 2027
| 4/10 (four 10-hour days) | 2,080 | 208 shifts of 10 hours
| Pitman, Panama, DuPont (12 hours) | 2,184 | 182 shifts of 12 hours
| 2 on 2 off (12 hours) | 2,196 | 183 shifts of 12 hours
| Southern swing (8 hours, rotating) | 2,184 | 273 shifts of 8 hours
| 24/72 (24 hours, four platoons) | 2,184 | 91 shifts of 24 hours
| 24/48 (24 hours, three platoons) | 2,928 | 122 shifts of 24 hours
| 48/96 (24 hours) | 2,928 | 122 shifts of 24 hours
| Kelly (24 hours) | 2,904 | 121 shifts of 24 hours
One crew, cycle starting Monday, January 4, 2027, before overtime, leave, Kelly days and swaps. Another crew or start date can move the total by one shift.
Four-crew 12-hour schedules average 42 hours a week, which is 2,184 a year: about 100 hours more than a weekday job, usually paid as overtime in the weeks with four shifts. Three-platoon fire schedules average 56 hours a week. Put your own pattern and start date in the shift calendar to count your year, or see the pay in the shift pay calculator.
Part-time and other weekly hours
| | Hours a week | Hours a year (× 52)
| 20 | 1,040
| 24 | 1,248
| 30 | 1,560
| 32 | 1,664
| 36 | 1,872
| 37.5 | 1,950
| 40 | 2,080
| 42 | 2,184
| 48 | 2,496
Three 12-hour shifts a week, the usual hospital contract, is 36 hours: 1,872 a year. For what counts as full time, see 12-hour shift schedules and the nurse schedules.
From hourly pay to a yearly salary
Multiply your hourly rate by your yearly hours. At $25 an hour, 2,080 hours is $52,000; 2,088 hours is $52,200; a 12-hour rotation at 2,184 hours is $54,600 before any overtime premium. If you are paid every two weeks, 2027 can also bring a 27th paycheck: see the 2027 pay period calendar.

Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
Is there 2,080 working hours in a year?
2,080 is the standard figure: 40 hours × 52 weeks. A calendar year has 52 weeks and one or two days, so most years have 2,088 weekday hours (261 weekdays × 8). 2027 has 2,088 and 2028 has 2,080.
How many working days are there in 2027?
261 weekdays. Without the 11 federal holidays, 253. Federal employees also get Friday, December 31, 2027 off for New Year's Day 2028, which leaves 249 working days.
How many hours are there in the year 2027?
8,760 hours: 365 days × 24 hours. 2028 is a leap year, with 8,784.
How many work hours are in a month?
173.3 on average (2,080 ÷ 12). A month with 23 weekdays has 184 hours at 8 a day, and February 2027, with 20 weekdays, has 160.
How many hours a year is a 12-hour shift schedule?
About 2,184 on four-crew schedules such as the Pitman, Panama and DuPont: 182 shifts of 12 hours, or 42 hours a week on average.
Why does the federal government divide by 2,087?
Because 2,087 is the long-run average of weekday hours in a year. 5 U.S.C. 5504(b) uses it to turn an annual salary into an hourly rate.

## 1st, 2nd and 3rd Shift Hours: What Time Each Shift Starts
URL: https://crewdays.app/first-second-third-shift-hours/

Home / Guides / 1st, 2nd and 3rd shift hours
1st, 2nd and 3rd shift hours
On 8-hour shifts, first shift usually runs from 7 a.m. to 3 p.m., second shift from 3 p.m. to 11 p.m. and third shift, the graveyard shift, from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. Many workplaces start an hour earlier or later. With 12-hour shifts there are only two: days and nights.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @sulyok_imaging on Unsplash
Common shift times
| | Shift | Also called | Common 8-hour times | Other common starts
| 1st shift | Day shift | 7 a.m. – 3 p.m. | 6 a.m. – 2 p.m., 8 a.m. – 4 p.m.
| 2nd shift | Evening, afternoon or swing shift | 3 p.m. – 11 p.m. | 2 p.m. – 10 p.m., 4 p.m. – midnight
| 3rd shift | Night, overnight or graveyard shift | 11 p.m. – 7 a.m. | 10 p.m. – 6 a.m., midnight – 8 a.m.
No federal law defines the shifts or their hours: the employer sets them. The three shifts always join up, so whatever time first shift starts, third shift ends there and the plant or ward is covered around the clock with three 8-hour crews. A fourth shift, where it exists, is usually a weekend crew or a relief crew that covers the others' days off.
10-hour and 12-hour shifts
With 10-hour shifts the day does not divide evenly, so the shifts overlap. A common police pattern is 6 a.m. – 4 p.m., 2 p.m. – midnight and 9 p.m. – 7 a.m., with the extra officers on the busiest hours of the evening.
With 12-hour shifts the day splits in two: 7 a.m. – 7 p.m. and 7 p.m. – 7 a.m. are the most common, or 6 to 6. Hospitals, police and most 24/7 plants on 12-hour rotations call them day shift and night shift rather than first and second. Each crew works about half the days of the year on a Pitman, DuPont or similar rotation.
Graveyard shift hours
Graveyard shift is another name for the third shift, the one that covers the small hours. On 8-hour shifts that is usually 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. or midnight to 8 a.m.; on 12-hour shifts the night shift, 7 p.m. to 7 a.m., covers it. A shift that ends at 3 a.m. is a late second shift in most workplaces, not a graveyard shift.
What time is considered night shift?
No single legal definition exists: each employer sets its own, and third shift usually runs from about 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. The federal government's pay rules give a useful benchmark. Federal wage-grade (blue-collar) employees get a night differential of 7.5% when most of their scheduled hours fall between 3 p.m. and midnight, and 10% when most fall between 11 p.m. and 8 a.m. (5 U.S.C. 5343(f)). For General Schedule employees, night work is regularly scheduled work between 6 p.m. and 6 a.m., paid at 10% extra (5 U.S.C. 5545(a)).
Do you get paid more for 2nd or 3rd shift?
Only if your employer or union contract says so. The Fair Labor Standards Act “does not require extra pay for night work” (U.S. Department of Labor). Many employers still pay a shift differential, either a fixed amount per hour or a percentage. When they do, it becomes part of your regular rate, so your overtime rate goes up with it (29 CFR 778.207(b)). Turn on “Your pay” in the shift calendar to add a night differential to your year.
Night shifts that cross midnight
A third shift starts on one date and ends on the next. For pay, each hour belongs to the workweek in which it is worked, so a shift that runs from Saturday night into Sunday can be split between two workweeks if your workweek starts at midnight on Sunday. In the Crewdays calendar each shift is shown on the day it starts.
Meal breaks count the same way at night as in the day: a bona fide meal period, ordinarily 30 minutes or more with no duties at all, is not work time (29 CFR 785.19). An 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. shift with an unpaid half hour is 7.5 paid hours. On the night the clocks change, an 8-hour night shift lasts 9 hours in November and 7 in March; see night shift and daylight saving time.
Which shift can teenagers work?
Federal child labor rules keep 14- and 15-year-olds to the hours between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m., or 9 p.m. from June 1 to Labor Day, and outside school hours (29 CFR 570.35). That rules out most second shifts and every third shift. The federal hour limits stop at 16, though many states set their own for 16- and 17-year-olds.
What is a rotating shift?
A rotating shift means your crew moves between shift times instead of keeping the same hours. In hospitals it usually means switching between 12-hour days and nights, as on the Panama or the rotating 4 on 4 off. Some plants rotate crews through all three 8-hour shifts: a week of days, a week of evenings and a week of nights. The southern swing is the classic version for four crews: 7 day shifts, 2 off, 7 evenings, 2 off, 7 nights and 3 off, a 28-day cycle. In 2027 one crew works 273 shifts (2,184 hours), a third of them on each shift. Choose “Southern swing” in the shift calendar to see your year, or compare other options on 24/7 shift schedules.

5-5-4 schedule
3-4-4-3 schedule
12-hour schedule with 3 crews
Southern swing schedule
8-hour schedule, every other weekend off

Questions
What time is 1st, 2nd and 3rd shift?
Usually 7 a.m. to 3 p.m., 3 p.m. to 11 p.m. and 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. on 8-hour shifts. Many employers start an hour earlier (6, 2 and 10) or later (8, 4 and midnight).
What is 2nd shift?
The evening shift, between day shift and night shift. On 8-hour shifts it usually runs from 3 p.m. to 11 p.m. It is also called the afternoon or swing shift.
What hours is a graveyard shift?
The overnight shift, usually 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. or midnight to 8 a.m. on 8-hour shifts, and 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. on 12-hour shifts.
Is 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. a graveyard shift?
It is the night shift on a 12-hour schedule and covers the graveyard hours. Workplaces on 12-hour shifts usually call it nights.
What is 4th shift?
There is no standard meaning. It is usually a weekend crew (for example Friday to Sunday on 12-hour shifts) or a relief crew that covers the other shifts' days off.
Do you get paid more for working 3rd shift?
Not by federal law: the FLSA does not require extra pay for night work. Many employers and union contracts pay a night differential, and it then counts in your overtime rate.

## Swing Shift: Hours, Meaning and Swing Shift Schedules
URL: https://crewdays.app/swing-shift/

Home / Guides / Swing shift
Swing shift: hours and schedules
Swing shift has two meanings. In most job ads it is the evening shift between day and night shift, usually 3 p.m. to 11 p.m. In plants, police and hospitals a swing shift schedule is one where your crew swings between day shifts and night shifts.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @ivorycirrus on Unsplash
Swing shift hours
As the evening shift, swing shift sits between day shift and the overnight shift. The common hours are:
| | Shift length | Common swing shift hours
| 8 hours | 3 p.m. – 11 p.m., 2 p.m. – 10 p.m. or 4 p.m. – midnight
| 10 hours | 2 p.m. – midnight or 4 p.m. – 2 a.m., overlapping the day and night shifts
| 12 hours | There is no evening shift: days and nights only (7 to 7 or 6 to 6)
The employer sets the hours; no federal rule defines them. For the other two shifts, see 1st, 2nd and 3rd shift hours.
What a swing shift schedule is
The second meaning is a rotation. On a swing shift schedule your crew works some weeks on days and some on nights, instead of staying on one shift. Job ads say “rotating shifts” or “12-hour swing shifts” for the same thing. It shares the night shifts fairly between crews, and everyone takes turns on the less popular hours.
The price is the change itself. Every swing from days to nights means moving your sleep by about 12 hours, and the first days off after a run of nights go partly to recovery. Schedules differ mostly in how often you swing and how many days off you get around the change.
12-hour swing shift schedules compared
These rotations all use four crews on 12-hour shifts, average 42 hours a week and give one crew on days and one on nights every day. For one crew in 2027:
| | Schedule | Cycle | Most shifts of one kind in a row | Day shifts | Night shifts | Full weekends off
| Panama (rotating 2-2-3) | 28 days | 3 | 91 | 91 | 26
| DuPont | 28 days | 4 | 91 | 91 | 26
| 4 on 4 off, rotating | 16 days | 4 | 92 | 90 | 21
| 3 on 3 off, rotating | 12 days | 3 | 92 | 90 | 17
| 2 on 2 off, rotating | 8 days | 2 | 92 | 91 | 13
| 7 on 7 off, rotating | 28 days | 7 | 91 | 91 | 26
| Continental (2 days, 2 nights, 4 off) | 8 days | 2 | 92 | 90 | 21
One crew, cycle starting Monday, January 4, 2027. A full weekend is Saturday and Sunday both off.
The Panama and 7 on 7 off swing every two weeks, so you have long runs on one shift. The 2 on 2 off and continental swing every few days, so your body never fully settles on nights, but each run of nights is short. The DuPont mixes blocks of three and four. Choose any of them in the shift calendar and pick “All crews” to see who is on days and who is on nights each day.
The southern swing: 8-hour shifts through all three
The southern swing rotates four crews through days, evenings and nights on 8-hour shifts: 7 days, 2 off, 7 evenings, 2 off, 7 nights and 3 off, a 28-day cycle. In 2027 one crew works 273 shifts: 91 days, 91 evenings and 91 nights, 2,184 hours in all. Full weekends off are rare, 13 in the year, because the only breaks are two or three days. Compare it with other 8-hour options on 24/7 shift schedules.
Swing shift pay
Federal law does not require a premium for evening or night work; the Fair Labor Standards Act leaves it to the employer and the employee or union (U.S. Department of Labor). Where a swing or night differential is paid, it counts toward the regular rate used for overtime (29 CFR 778.207(b)). As a benchmark, federal wage-grade employees get 7.5% extra for shifts that fall mostly between 3 p.m. and midnight and 10% for shifts mostly between 11 p.m. and 8 a.m. (5 U.S.C. 5343(f)).
On a rotating schedule only part of your shifts carry a night differential, so yearly pay depends on how many nights the rotation gives you. The table above counts them; the pay estimate in the shift calendar adds the differential for your own dates.
Living with a swing shift
A few habits make rotating easier. Plan the first day off after nights as a recovery day, not a day for errands. Keep the same sleep window for the whole run of nights, including the days in between if you have only one off. Share the calendar with your family so the swing weeks are no surprise: the shift calendar gives a link that opens on any phone. On the night the clocks change, a 12-hour night shift lasts 13 or 11 hours; see daylight saving time on night shift.

Questions
What hours are usually swing shift?
As the evening shift, usually 3 p.m. to 11 p.m. on 8-hour shifts, or 2 p.m. to 10 p.m. or 4 p.m. to midnight. The employer sets the exact times.
What does swing shift mean?
Either the evening shift, between day and night shift, or a schedule where your crew rotates between day and night shifts.
What is a 2-2-3 swing shift schedule?
A Pitman-type 12-hour rotation (2 on, 2 off, 3 on, 2 off, 2 on, 3 off) where crews swing between days and nights, usually every two weeks. With that swing it is called the Panama schedule.
What is a 12-hour swing shift schedule?
A 12-hour rotation in which each crew works both day and night shifts, such as the Panama, DuPont, rotating 4 on 4 off or 2 on 2 off. Four crews cover 24/7 at 42 hours a week on average.
Why is it called swing shift?
The name refers to a shift that swings between the others: the evening shift falls between day and night shift, and a rotating crew swings between days and nights.
Is swing shift paid more?
Only if the employer or union contract pays a differential; federal law does not require one. When it is paid, it raises the overtime rate too.

## Time Calculator: Add and Subtract Hours and Minutes
URL: https://crewdays.app/time-calculator/

Home / Guides / Time calculator
Time calculator
Add or subtract hours and minutes, or add a length of time to a clock time to see when a shift ends, even past midnight. The answer comes in hours and minutes and in decimal hours for payroll.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Add or subtract hours and minutes
Photo: @the9th on Unsplash
What time will it be after a number of hours?
How to add hours and minutes by hand
Add the hours and the minutes separately. If the minutes come to 60 or more, take 60 away and add one hour. For example, 7:45 + 4:30 is 11 hours and 75 minutes, which is 12:15. To subtract, borrow an hour when you need it: 12:15 − 4:30 is 11:75 − 4:30, which is 7:45.
For a clock time, add the length of the shift to the start and take 24 hours away if you pass midnight. A 12-hour night shift that starts at 7:00 p.m. ends at 7:00 a.m. the next day; add 30 minutes of unpaid break and it ends at 7:30 a.m.
Minutes to decimal hours
Payroll systems usually want hours as a decimal. Divide the minutes by 60:
| | Minutes | Decimal hours | Minutes | Decimal hours
| 5 | .08 | 35 | .58
| 10 | .17 | 40 | .67
| 15 | .25 | 45 | .75
| 20 | .33 | 50 | .83
| 25 | .42 | 55 | .92
| 30 | .50 | 60 | 1.00
So 7 hours 45 minutes is 7.75 hours, and 11 hours 20 minutes is 11.33 hours.
Rounding on time clocks
Many employers round punches to the nearest 5 minutes, tenth of an hour (6 minutes) or quarter hour (15 minutes). Federal rules accept this only if it averages out, so that over time employees are paid for all the time they actually work (29 CFR 785.48(b)). Rounding that always favours the employer does not meet that test.
More time tools
To total a whole week of punches with overtime, use the time card calculator. For the hours between a start and end time, the hours calculator; for a 24-hour clock, the military time chart. Shift patterns and their yearly hours are in the shift calendar.

Salary calculator
Tax calculator
Military time chart
Sleep calculator
Hours calculator
All guides
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
How do I add hours and minutes?
Add hours and minutes separately, then turn every 60 minutes into an hour. 7:45 plus 4:30 is 11 hours 75 minutes, which is 12 hours 15 minutes.
How do I subtract time?
Subtract the minutes first. If you do not have enough, borrow an hour as 60 minutes. 12:15 minus 4:30 is 11:75 minus 4:30, which is 7:45.
What is 45 minutes as a decimal?
0.75 hours. Divide the minutes by 60: 15 minutes is 0.25, 30 minutes is 0.5 and 45 minutes is 0.75.
What time is it 12 hours after 7 p.m.?
7 a.m. the next day. Add the hours to the start time and take 24 away when you pass midnight.
Is rounding time clock punches legal?
Under federal rules, rounding to the nearest 5, 6 or 15 minutes is accepted only if over time it does not leave employees unpaid for time they worked (29 CFR 785.48(b)).

## Hours Calculator: Hours Worked Between Two Times
URL: https://crewdays.app/hours-calculator/

Home / Guides / Hours calculator
Hours calculator
Enter when you started and finished and any unpaid break. The calculator gives the hours worked in hours and minutes and in decimal, works across midnight for night shifts and, if you add your hourly rate, shows the pay.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @joshua_hoehne on Unsplash
Hours for common shifts
| | Shift | Hours | With a 30-minute unpaid meal
| 9:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. | 8 | 7.5
| 8:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. | 8.5 | 8
| 7:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m. | 8 | 7.5
| 3:00 p.m. – 11:00 p.m. | 8 | 7.5
| 11:00 p.m. – 7:00 a.m. | 8 | 7.5
| 7:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m. | 12 | 11.5
| 7:00 p.m. – 7:00 a.m. | 12 | 11.5
| 6:00 a.m. – 6:30 p.m. | 12.5 | 12
A shift that ends earlier on the clock than it started has crossed midnight: the calculator adds 24 hours to the end time before subtracting.
Which breaks count as hours worked?
Under federal rules, short rest breaks of about 5 to 20 minutes are work time and must be paid (29 CFR 785.18). A meal period is unpaid only when you are completely relieved of duty, ordinarily for 30 minutes or more; if you eat at your station or answer calls, it counts as work (29 CFR 785.19). So only enter breaks that you take off duty. Several states also require meal or rest breaks; your state labor department has the details.
How to calculate hours worked by hand
Write both times on the 24-hour clock: 10:45 p.m. is 22:45 and 7:15 a.m. is 07:15.
Subtract the start from the end. If the result is negative, the shift crossed midnight: add 24 hours. 07:15 − 22:45 is −15:30, plus 24:00 is 8:30.
Take off any unpaid meal break: 8:30 − 0:30 is 8 hours.
For payroll, turn the minutes into a decimal: 30 minutes is 0.5, so 8:30 is 8.5 hours.
For a week, add the days and compare with 40. Three 12-hour shifts and one 8-hour day make 44 hours: 40 regular and 4 overtime at time and a half under federal law. The military time chart helps with step 1.
Decimal hours for payroll
To pay hours and minutes, turn the minutes into a decimal by dividing by 60: 11 hours 30 minutes is 11.5 hours. At $25 an hour that is $287.50. Every quarter hour is 0.25.
Totals for a week or a year
For several days at once and weekly overtime, use the time card calculator. To count a year of shifts on a rotating schedule, put your pattern in the shift calendar; the work hours in a year guide compares 8, 12 and 24-hour schedules.

Questions
How many hours is 9 to 5?
8 hours. With an unpaid 30-minute lunch it is 7.5 hours, and with an unpaid hour 7 hours.
How many hours is 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.?
12 hours. With a 30-minute unpaid meal break, 11.5 paid hours.
How many hours is 7 p.m. to 7 a.m.?
12 hours. When the end time is earlier than the start, the shift crosses midnight: add 24 hours to the end before subtracting.
How many hours is 8 to 4:30?
8.5 hours, or 8 hours with a 30-minute unpaid lunch.
Do breaks count as hours worked?
Rest breaks of about 5 to 20 minutes do and must be paid. Meal periods of 30 minutes or more are unpaid only if you are completely relieved of duty (29 CFR 785.18 and 785.19).

## Time Card Calculator With Breaks and Overtime
URL: https://crewdays.app/time-card-calculator/

Home / Guides / Time card calculator
Time card calculator
Fill in your clock-in and clock-out times and unpaid breaks for each day. The calculator totals the week, splits regular hours from overtime over 40 and works out pay at time and a half. Night shifts that end after midnight count on the day they start.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @99up on Unsplash
How overtime is counted
Federal law requires overtime of at least one and a half times the regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek (29 CFR 778.107). The workweek is a fixed period of 168 hours that the employer chooses, and each week stands alone: hours are not averaged over two weeks (29 CFR 778.104). The example above, four 12-hour shifts with a 30-minute break, comes to 46 hours: 40 regular and 6 overtime.
Some states add daily overtime. California pays time and a half after 8 hours in a day and double time after 12; Alaska pays after 8 hours a day; Colorado after 12. The shift pay calculator applies those rules to a whole year of shifts.
Night differential and the overtime rate
If you are paid a shift differential, it is part of your regular rate, so the overtime rate rises with it (29 CFR 778.207(b)). This calculator uses one hourly rate; read shift hours and night pay for how the differential works.
Time card tips
Record the actual times you started and stopped work; rounding is accepted only if it averages out over time (29 CFR 785.48).
Only take off breaks you spent completely off duty; short rest breaks are paid time.
Keep your own copy of each week: it is the quickest way to check a paycheck.

Time calculator
Paycheck calculator
Salary calculator
Tax calculator
Military time chart
Sleep calculator
All guides
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
How do I calculate hours on a time card?
For each day subtract the clock-in time from the clock-out time, take off unpaid breaks, then add the days. Turn minutes into decimals by dividing by 60.
How do you calculate a night shift on a time card?
If the out time is earlier than the in time, the shift crossed midnight: add 24 hours to the out time. A shift from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. is 12 hours.
When does overtime start?
Under federal law, after 40 hours in the workweek, at one and a half times the regular rate. Some states also pay daily overtime, such as California after 8 hours.
Are breaks paid?
Rest breaks of about 5 to 20 minutes are paid work time. Meal periods of 30 minutes or more can be unpaid if you are completely relieved of duty.
Can overtime be averaged over two weeks?
No. Each workweek stands alone under federal law (29 CFR 778.104). Hospitals can use the 8/80 system instead, with overtime after 8 hours a day and 80 in 14 days.

## Military Time Chart and Converter (24-Hour Clock)
URL: https://crewdays.app/military-time-chart/

Home / Guides / Military time chart
Military time chart
Military time counts the hours from 00 to 23, so there is no a.m. or p.m.: 0700 is 7 a.m. and 1900 is 7 p.m. For any hour after noon, take away 12 to get the regular time, or add 12 to go the other way.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @okcdz on Unsplash
Military time chart
| | Military | Regular | Military | Regular
| 0000 | 12:00 a.m. | 0030 | 12:30 a.m.
| 0100 | 1:00 a.m. | 0130 | 1:30 a.m.
| 0200 | 2:00 a.m. | 0230 | 2:30 a.m.
| 0300 | 3:00 a.m. | 0330 | 3:30 a.m.
| 0400 | 4:00 a.m. | 0430 | 4:30 a.m.
| 0500 | 5:00 a.m. | 0530 | 5:30 a.m.
| 0600 | 6:00 a.m. | 0630 | 6:30 a.m.
| 0700 | 7:00 a.m. | 0730 | 7:30 a.m.
| 0800 | 8:00 a.m. | 0830 | 8:30 a.m.
| 0900 | 9:00 a.m. | 0930 | 9:30 a.m.
| 1000 | 10:00 a.m. | 1030 | 10:30 a.m.
| 1100 | 11:00 a.m. | 1130 | 11:30 a.m.
| 1200 | 12:00 p.m. | 1230 | 12:30 p.m.
| 1300 | 1:00 p.m. | 1330 | 1:30 p.m.
| 1400 | 2:00 p.m. | 1430 | 2:30 p.m.
| 1500 | 3:00 p.m. | 1530 | 3:30 p.m.
| 1600 | 4:00 p.m. | 1630 | 4:30 p.m.
| 1700 | 5:00 p.m. | 1730 | 5:30 p.m.
| 1800 | 6:00 p.m. | 1830 | 6:30 p.m.
| 1900 | 7:00 p.m. | 1930 | 7:30 p.m.
| 2000 | 8:00 p.m. | 2030 | 8:30 p.m.
| 2100 | 9:00 p.m. | 2130 | 9:30 p.m.
| 2200 | 10:00 p.m. | 2230 | 10:30 p.m.
| 2300 | 11:00 p.m. | 2330 | 11:30 p.m.
How to read military time
The first two digits are the hour and the last two the minutes. From 0100 to 1259 the hours match the morning clock (0930 is 9:30 a.m.). From 1300 to 2359, subtract 12 from the hour (1745 is 5:45 p.m.). Midnight is 0000, the start of the day; some schedules write 2400 for midnight at the end of a day, so a night shift may show as 1900 to 0700 or 1900 to 2400 and 0000 to 0700.
People usually say it as two pairs: 0700 is “oh seven hundred” or “zero seven hundred”, 1930 is “nineteen thirty”, and the hours are often followed by “hours”.
Common mistakes
Noon and midnight. 1200 is noon and 0000 is midnight. 12:30 a.m., half an hour after midnight, is 0030, not 1230.
Adding hours. Military time is still in hours and minutes: 1745 plus 30 minutes is 1815, not 1775.
Decimal hours. Payroll often uses decimals: a shift from 0645 to 1915 is 12 hours 30 minutes, 12.5 hours. The hours calculator does it for you.
Time zones. The same clock reading means a different moment in another zone; aviation and IT logs use UTC, written with a Z. See UTC time.
Military time on shift schedules
Hospitals, police, fire departments and plants write shift times on the 24-hour clock because it removes any doubt about a.m. and p.m. A 12-hour rotation usually runs 0700–1900 and 1900–0700; 8-hour shifts often run 0700–1500, 1500–2300 and 2300–0700. See 1st, 2nd and 3rd shift hours. To total hours on a time card that uses the 24-hour clock, use the hours calculator.
Military and aviation schedules also add a time zone letter. “Z”, or Zulu time, means Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Questions
What time is 1700 in military time?
5:00 p.m. Subtract 12 from any hour above 12.
What is 2100 in regular time?
9:00 p.m.
How do you write midnight in military time?
0000 at the start of the day. Some schedules use 2400 for midnight at the end of a day.
What is 12:30 a.m. in military time?
0030. The hour after midnight is 00.
How do you convert p.m. to military time?
Add 12 to the hour, except for 12 noon: 3:15 p.m. is 1515 and 12:45 p.m. is 1245.

## Hourly Paycheck Calculator 2026 With Overtime
URL: https://crewdays.app/paycheck-calculator/

Home / Guides / Paycheck calculator
Hourly paycheck calculator
Enter your hourly rate, hours and overtime for one pay period. The calculator adds any shift differential, then takes off Social Security, Medicare, an estimate of federal income tax with the 2026 IRS brackets and, if you enter one, a state tax rate.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @moneyknack on Unsplash
What comes out of a paycheck
| | Deduction | 2026 rate | Source
| Social Security | 6.2% of wages up to $184,500 a year | SSA
| Medicare | 1.45% of all wages, plus 0.9% withheld on wages over $200,000 | IRS Topic 751
| Federal income tax | 10% to 37% after the standard deduction ($16,100 single, $32,200 married filing jointly) | IRS
| State and local tax | Depends on the state; some, such as Texas and Florida, have no income tax on wages | Your state
The federal income tax here is an estimate: the calculator annualizes your gross pay, takes off the standard deduction and applies the 2026 brackets. Your real withholding follows your Form W-4 and the IRS tables, and credits such as the child tax credit lower it further. Use it to plan, not to file.
Overtime and shift differential
Overtime here is paid at time and a half for every hour you enter as overtime. Federal law requires it after 40 hours in a workweek. On a 12-hour rotation, a two-week pay period of 84 hours can carry anything from 0 to 8 or more overtime hours, depending on how the shifts fall in each week. A differential raises your regular rate, which raises the overtime rate too (29 CFR 778.207(b)). To see every paycheck of the year on your own rotation, use the shift pay calculator or the pay option in the shift calendar.
The overtime deduction
From 2025 to 2028 you can deduct the extra half of qualified overtime pay (the part above your regular rate) when you file. The limit is $12,500 a year, or $25,000 filing jointly, phased out above $150,000 of modified adjusted gross income ($300,000 jointly). You need a valid Social Security number and married couples must file jointly (IRS). It does not reduce Social Security or Medicare. Choose “Yes” above to see its effect on the yearly tax spread over each paycheck; your employer's withholding may not include it.

Salary calculator
Tax calculator
Military time chart
Sleep calculator
Hours calculator
Time card calculator
All guides
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
How much is taken out of a paycheck in 2026?
Social Security is 6.2% (up to $184,500 of wages), Medicare 1.45%, plus federal income tax that depends on your income and W-4, and state tax where it applies. For many hourly workers the total is roughly 15% to 25% of gross pay.
How do I calculate my paycheck from my hourly rate?
Multiply your rate by your regular hours, add overtime hours at 1.5 times the rate and any differential, then subtract Social Security, Medicare and income taxes.
Is overtime taxed more?
No. Overtime is added to your pay and taxed at the same rates. It can push the paycheck into a higher withholding bracket, but the tax is settled on your yearly income when you file.
What is the standard deduction for 2026?
$16,100 for single filers, $32,200 for married couples filing jointly and $24,150 for heads of household (IRS).
Does the no tax on overtime deduction lower my paycheck taxes?
It is claimed on your tax return (Schedule 1-A), for the overtime premium only, up to $12,500 or $25,000 jointly. It does not reduce Social Security or Medicare tax.

---

## Salary Calculator: Hourly to Annual Pay (2026)
URL: https://crewdays.app/salary-calculator/

Home / Guides / Salary calculator
Salary calculator: hourly to yearly
Multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work in a week and by 52. At 40 hours a week, $25 an hour is $52,000 a year. Change the hours to match your shift schedule: 36 for three 12s, 42 for a 12-hour rotation and 56 for a 24/48.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @alexandermils on Unsplash
Hourly to salary table
| | Hourly | 40 h a week (2,080 h) | 36 h (three 12s) | 42 h (12-hour rotation) | Monthly at 40 h
| $15 | $31,200 | $28,080 | $32,760 | $2,600.00
| $18 | $37,440 | $33,696 | $39,312 | $3,120.00
| $20 | $41,600 | $37,440 | $43,680 | $3,466.67
| $22 | $45,760 | $41,184 | $48,048 | $3,813.33
| $25 | $52,000 | $46,800 | $54,600 | $4,333.33
| $28 | $58,240 | $52,416 | $61,152 | $4,853.33
| $30 | $62,400 | $56,160 | $65,520 | $5,200.00
| $35 | $72,800 | $65,520 | $76,440 | $6,066.67
| $40 | $83,200 | $74,880 | $87,360 | $6,933.33
| $45 | $93,600 | $84,240 | $98,280 | $7,800.00
| $50 | $104,000 | $93,600 | $109,200 | $8,666.67
Before tax and without overtime premium. 2,184 hours is the average of a four-crew 12-hour schedule such as the Pitman or DuPont; the extra hours are often paid as overtime, so the real figure is higher. At the federal minimum of $7.25, a 40-hour week is $15,080 a year; most states pay more (see the minimum wage by state).
Salary to hourly
Divide the yearly salary by the hours you work in a year: by 2,080 for a 40-hour week. $60,000 a year is $28.85 an hour; $75,000 is $36.06. Federal agencies divide by 2,087 instead, the long-run average of weekday hours (5 U.S.C. 5504(b)). See work hours in a year for why 2027 has 2,088.
Weekly, biweekly or twice a month?
The same salary gives different paychecks depending on how often you are paid. A $52,000 salary is $1,000 a week, $2,000 every two weeks (26 paychecks), $2,166.67 twice a month (24 paychecks) or $4,333.33 a month. Biweekly and twice-a-month sound alike but differ by two paychecks a year. In a year with 27 biweekly paydays, as some payrolls have in 2027, hourly workers get one more check; salaried workers should ask whether the employer divides the salary by 26 or by 27. See the 2027 pay period calendar.
From gross salary to take-home pay
Take $25 an hour at 40 hours a week: $52,000 a year. A single filer in 2026 pays about $3,978 in Social Security and Medicare (7.65%) and about $4,060 in federal income tax after the $16,100 standard deduction. That leaves about $43,962 before any state tax. The tax calculator shows the brackets and the paycheck calculator splits it per paycheck.
A night differential adds up quickly: $2 an hour extra on half of the 2,184 hours of a 12-hour rotation is $2,184 a year, and it also raises the overtime rate.
Shift workers: count the overtime
On a 12-hour rotation the weeks are uneven, so some weeks pass 40 hours and pay overtime even though the average is 42. Depending on the day your employer's workweek starts, a Pitman crew can work anything from about 208 to 520 overtime hours a year. The shift pay calculator adds that overtime for your pattern, and the paycheck calculator shows take-home pay.

Questions
$25 an hour is how much a year?
$52,000 at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks, before tax. On a 12-hour rotation averaging 42 hours a week it is $54,600 before overtime premium.
$20 an hour is how much a year?
$41,600 at 40 hours a week. That is $3,466.67 a month or $1,600 every two weeks.
How do I convert my salary to an hourly rate?
Divide the yearly salary by 2,080 (40 hours × 52 weeks). $50,000 a year is $24.04 an hour.
How many hours a year is full time?
2,080 is the standard figure (40 hours × 52 weeks). Calendar years have 2,080 to 2,096 weekday hours; 2027 has 2,088.
Should I count unpaid time off?
Yes. If you take two weeks of unpaid leave, use 50 weeks instead of 52.

## Federal Income Tax Calculator 2026 (With Brackets)
URL: https://crewdays.app/tax-calculator/

Home / Guides / Tax calculator
Federal income tax calculator 2026
Enter your yearly income and filing status. The calculator takes off the 2026 standard deduction ($16,100 single, $32,200 married filing jointly) and the overtime deduction if you have one, then applies the 2026 tax brackets published by the IRS.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @kellysikkema on Unsplash
2026 federal tax brackets
| | Rate | Single (taxable income) | Married filing jointly
| 10% | $0 – $12,400 | $0 – $24,800
| 12% | $12,400 – $50,400 | $24,800 – $100,800
| 22% | $50,400 – $105,700 | $100,800 – $211,400
| 24% | $105,700 – $201,775 | $211,400 – $403,550
| 32% | $201,775 – $256,225 | $403,550 – $512,450
| 35% | $256,225 – $640,600 | $512,450 – $768,700
| 37% | over $640,600 | over $768,700
Source: IRS, tax year 2026 inflation adjustments. The rates apply to taxable income, after the standard deduction. Each rate only applies to the part of your income inside its bracket, so moving into a higher bracket never lowers your take-home pay.
How the calculation works
With $60,000 of wages as a single filer, taxable income is $60,000 − $16,100 = $43,900. The first $12,400 is taxed at 10% ($1,240) and the remaining $31,500 at 12% ($3,780), so the tax is $5,020: about 8.4% of income, with a top bracket of 12%. Credits, other income and itemized deductions change the result; this is an estimate for planning, not a return.
The deduction for overtime
For 2025 to 2028 you can deduct qualified overtime compensation: the pay above your regular rate for overtime hours, that is, the extra “half” of time and a half. The maximum is $12,500 a year, or $25,000 filing jointly, and it phases out above $150,000 of modified adjusted gross income ($300,000 jointly). It is claimed on Schedule 1-A whether you itemize or not (IRS). Enter that premium above; for 200 overtime hours at $25 an hour it is 200 × $12.50 = $2,500. Shift workers can find their overtime hours for a year in the shift pay calculator.
Payroll taxes are separate
Social Security (6.2% up to $184,500 of wages) and Medicare (1.45%) come out of every paycheck on top of income tax. The paycheck calculator shows all of them for one pay period.

Questions
What are the 2026 tax brackets?
For single filers: 10% up to $12,400 of taxable income, 12% to $50,400, 22% to $105,700, 24% to $201,775, 32% to $256,225, 35% to $640,600 and 37% above. Married couples filing jointly have brackets twice as wide up to 35%.
What is the 2026 standard deduction?
$16,100 for single filers, $32,200 for married filing jointly and $24,150 for heads of household.
How much federal tax do I pay on $60,000?
About $5,020 as a single filer using the standard deduction and no credits: about 8.4% of income.
How does the no tax on overtime deduction work?
You deduct the overtime premium (the pay above your regular rate), up to $12,500 or $25,000 for joint filers, for 2025 to 2028. It phases out above $150,000 of modified AGI ($300,000 jointly).
Does a raise ever lower my take-home pay because of the bracket?
No. A higher rate applies only to the income inside that bracket, not to all of it.

## Daylight Saving Time 2026: When Clocks Change (US and UK)
URL: https://crewdays.app/daylight-saving-time/

Home / Guides / Daylight saving time
Daylight saving time: when the clocks change
In the US, daylight saving time ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 2:00 a.m., when clocks go back one hour. It starts again on Sunday, March 14, 2027. In the UK, clocks go back on Sunday, October 25, 2026 and forward on March 28, 2027.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @adrienrobert on Unsplash
Daylight saving time dates
| | Year | US: clocks forward (2 a.m.) | US: clocks back (2 a.m.) | UK: forward (1 a.m. GMT) | UK: back (2 a.m. BST)
| 2026 | Sunday, March 8 | Sunday, November 1 | Sunday, March 29 | Sunday, October 25
| 2027 | Sunday, March 14 | Sunday, November 7 | Sunday, March 28 | Sunday, October 31
| 2028 | Sunday, March 12 | Sunday, November 5 | Sunday, March 26 | Sunday, October 29
| 2029 | Sunday, March 11 | Sunday, November 4 | Sunday, March 25 | Sunday, October 28
| 2030 | Sunday, March 10 | Sunday, November 3 | Sunday, March 31 | Sunday, October 27
The rule in the US
Federal law sets daylight saving time from 2:00 a.m. on the second Sunday of March to 2:00 a.m. on the first Sunday of November (15 U.S.C. 260a). A state can choose to stay on standard time all year; Hawaii and most of Arizona do. A state cannot adopt daylight saving time all year on its own under this law. In March, 2:00 a.m. jumps to 3:00 a.m.; in November, 2:00 a.m. becomes 1:00 a.m. again, so the hour from 1:00 to 2:00 happens twice.
The rule in the UK
British Summer Time runs from 1:00 a.m. GMT on the last Sunday in March to 1:00 a.m. GMT on the last Sunday in October (Summer Time Order 2002). In October the clocks go back from 2:00 a.m. BST to 1:00 a.m. GMT. Because the UK and US change on different Sundays, the time difference between London and New York is four hours instead of five for about three weeks in March and one week around the end of October.
Working a night shift when the clocks change
If you work through the change, your shift is one hour longer in the fall and one hour shorter in the spring. A 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. shift lasts 13 hours on November 1, 2026 and 11 hours on March 14, 2027. Under federal rules you are paid for the hours you actually work, so the extra hour in November counts toward your weekly overtime. The night shift and daylight saving time calculator works out your exact hours and pay.
Your body clock
Losing an hour in March feels like a short night for most people, and harder for anyone already short of sleep. The sleep calculator helps you plan bedtime around a set wake-up time. For calendars that do not move when the clocks change, the shift files from the shift calendar use all-day events.
