Questions
When does daylight saving time end in 2026?
On Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 2:00 a.m. in the US, when clocks go back one hour. In the UK, clocks go back on Sunday, October 25, 2026.
When does daylight saving time start in 2027?
On Sunday, March 14, 2027 at 2:00 a.m. in the US. In the UK, clocks go forward on Sunday, March 28, 2027.
Do we gain or lose an hour in November?
You gain one: at 2:00 a.m. the clock goes back to 1:00 a.m. In March you lose an hour.
Which states do not observe daylight saving time?
Hawaii and most of Arizona stay on standard time all year, as federal law allows (15 U.S.C. 260a).
Do I get paid for the extra hour on a night shift?
Hourly employees are paid for the hours they actually work, so a 12-hour night shift that lasts 13 hours in November is paid as 13 hours.

## Sleep Calculator: When to Go to Bed (Night Shift Too)
URL: https://crewdays.app/sleep-calculator/

Home / Guides / Sleep calculator
Sleep calculator
Sleep runs in cycles of about 90 minutes, and you wake up less groggy at the end of one. Enter your wake-up time to get bedtimes for 9, 7.5 or 6 hours of sleep, with 15 minutes to fall asleep. After a night shift, use the second calculator.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
I have to wake up at…
Photo: @solvinghealthcare on Unsplash
I'm going to bed at… (after a night shift)
How much sleep do adults need?
The CDC recommends 7 or more hours a day for adults aged 18 to 60, 7 to 9 hours from 61 to 64 and 7 to 8 hours from 65 (CDC). Five cycles (7.5 hours) is a good target for most people; four cycles (6 hours) is a short night, fine now and then but not every day.
Why 90 minutes?
Sleep gets deeper the longer you sleep and reaches its deepest stage in about an hour. NIOSH explains that waking from deep sleep brings “sleep inertia”, grogginess that can last a while, and that waking at about 90 minutes, at the predicted end of a sleep cycle, usually means less of it (NIOSH). Cycles vary from person to person, so treat the times as a guide and adjust by 15 minutes if you still wake up tired.
Sleeping after a night shift
After nights, the hardest part is sleeping in daylight. Go to bed as soon as you can after you get home, make the room dark and cool, and keep the same sleep window for every night of the run. For people on day schedules, NIOSH recommends a brief nap of under 20 minutes, with an alarm set for 15 to 30 minutes: it raises alertness for a couple of hours with little grogginess. Whatever your shift, waking up before you reach deep sleep, or after a full cycle of about 90 minutes, is what keeps the grogginess short.
Plan the swap back to days too: the first day off after a run of nights is partly a recovery day. See swing shift schedules for rotations that change between days and nights, and the clock change dates if you work through one.

Paycheck calculator
Salary calculator
Tax calculator

Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
What time should I go to bed if I wake up at 6:30?
For 7.5 hours of sleep (five cycles), at 10:45 p.m. For 9 hours, at 9:15 p.m., and for 6 hours, at 12:15 a.m. These times include 15 minutes to fall asleep.
How long is a sleep cycle?
About 90 minutes on average. NIOSH notes that waking at about 90 minutes, at the end of a cycle, usually means less grogginess.
How many hours of sleep do adults need?
7 or more hours a day for adults aged 18 to 60, according to the CDC.
How should I sleep after a night shift?
Go to bed soon after you get home, keep the room dark and cool and sleep at the same times on each day of the run. Plan for at least 7 hours.
How long should a nap be?
NIOSH says both short naps (15 to 30 minutes) and longer ones can increase alertness. Waking at about 20 minutes, before deep sleep, or at about 90 minutes, at the end of a cycle, means less grogginess.

## How Many Weeks in a Year? 52 (and 2026 Has 53 ISO Weeks)
URL: https://crewdays.app/how-many-weeks-in-a-year/

Home / Guides / Weeks in a year
How many weeks are in a year?
A year has 52 weeks and 1 day: 365 days divided by 7. A leap year has 52 weeks and 2 days. Week numbers are different: 2026 has 53 ISO weeks and 2027 has 52, because the count depends on the weekday the year starts.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @nate_dumlao on Unsplash
Weeks in each year
| | Year | Days | Weeks | Starts on | ISO week numbers
| 2025 | 365 | 52 weeks + 1 day | Wednesday | 52
| 2026 | 365 | 52 weeks + 1 day | Thursday | 53
| 2027 | 365 | 52 weeks + 1 day | Friday | 52
| 2028 | 366 | 52 weeks + 2 days | Saturday | 52
| 2029 | 365 | 52 weeks + 1 day | Monday | 52
| 2030 | 365 | 52 weeks + 1 day | Tuesday | 52
Why some years have 53 week numbers
The ISO 8601 standard, used by most calendars and payroll systems outside the US and by many plants, numbers weeks from Monday to Sunday. Week 1 is the week that contains the first Thursday of the year, so a year has 53 numbered weeks when it starts on a Thursday, or on a Wednesday in a leap year. 2026 starts on a Thursday, so it has week 53, which runs from December 28, 2026 to January 3, 2027.
US calendars often count weeks differently, starting on Sunday with January 1 always in week 1. Check which system your employer's schedule or payroll uses before you match week numbers.
Weeks and paychecks
52 weeks means 26 biweekly paychecks in most years. The extra day each year adds up, and every 11 years or so a biweekly payroll has 27 paydays in a calendar year. In 2027 there are 53 Fridays, so payrolls paid every other Friday starting on January 1, 2027 get 27 paychecks. The 2027 pay period calendar lists them.
Work weeks and hours
At 40 hours a week, 52 weeks is 2,080 work hours. Taking out two weeks of vacation leaves 50 working weeks and 2,000 hours. For the exact weekday count of each year and the hours of rotating shift schedules, see work hours in a year.

Questions
How many weeks are in a year?
52 weeks and 1 day (365 days), or 52 weeks and 2 days in a leap year (366 days).
Does 2026 have 53 weeks?
It has 53 ISO week numbers, because it starts on a Thursday. Week 53 runs from Monday, December 28, 2026 to Sunday, January 3, 2027. In days, 2026 has 52 weeks and 1 day like any normal year.
How many weeks are in 2027?
52 ISO weeks. 2027 starts on a Friday and has 365 days.
What week of the year is it?
Use the calculator above: it gives the ISO week number of any date. ISO weeks start on Monday and week 1 contains the first Thursday of the year.
How many work weeks are in a year?
52, or 50 if you take two weeks of vacation. At 40 hours a week, 52 weeks is 2,080 hours.

## Date Calculator: Days Between Dates and Add Days
URL: https://crewdays.app/date-calculator/

Home / Guides / Date calculator
Date calculator
Count the days between two dates, with how many of them are weekdays, or add or subtract days from a date to find a deadline. The first calculator starts from today.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Days between two dates
Photo: @behy_studio on Unsplash
Add or subtract days
Counting days: include the end date or not?
The calculator counts the days from the start date up to the end date, without counting the end date itself: from Monday to Friday of the same week is 4 days. If you need both days included, as when you count days of leave, add one. A period “of 30 days” starting on October 19 ends on November 17 if day 1 is October 19, and on November 18 if counting starts the next day; legal deadlines usually say which.
Weekdays and business days
Weekdays here are Monday to Friday. Business days also leave out holidays, which depend on your employer; the 11 US federal holidays are listed in work hours in a year. For shift workers, “days” in a contract or a rota usually means calendar days, since you work on weekends too.
Leap years and long periods
A leap year has 366 days, with February 29. The rule of the calendar we use is: years divisible by 4 are leap years, except years divisible by 100, which are leap years only if they are also divisible by 400. So 2028 is a leap year, 2100 will not be, and 2000 was. A period that includes February 29 is one day longer than the same dates in a normal year; from January 1 to December 31, 2027 is 364 days (365 counting both ends).
For week numbers, see how many weeks are in a year; for working days and hours, work hours in a year.
Dates on a shift rotation
Rotating schedules repeat every few days: 14 for a Pitman, 28 for a DuPont, 3 for a 24/48. To find whether you work on a given date, count the days from a day you know you started a block and divide by the cycle length; the remainder tells you where you are in the cycle. The shift calendar does this for every day of the year at once.

How many days until Christmas 2026?
From October 19, 2026 it is 67 days to December 25, 2026, not counting Christmas Day. The calculator above counts from today.
How do I count the days between two dates?
Subtract the start date from the end date. The result does not include the end date; add one day if you want to count both.

Use the second calculator: enter today and 90 days. From October 19, 2026 it is Sunday, January 17, 2027.

The calculator shows them: Monday to Friday, not counting the end date. Holidays are not taken out.
Does a 14-day notice include weekends?
Usually yes: notice periods are normally calendar days unless the contract or the law says working days.

Minimum wage by state (2026)
The federal minimum wage is $7.25 an hour, and it applies in 20 states that have no higher rate. The District of Columbia has the highest minimum, $18.40, followed by Washington ($17.13), Connecticut ($16.94) and California ($16.90), according to the US Department of Labor table updated on July 1, 2026.

Cities and counties can set higher rates, and tipped workers and some small employers have their own rules. Check your state labor department before relying on a figure.
The federal minimum wage
The Fair Labor Standards Act sets the federal minimum at $7.25 an hour (29 U.S.C. 206). Where a state or city sets a higher rate, the employer must pay the higher one. The federal law also requires overtime at one and a half times the regular rate after 40 hours in a workweek.
Minimum wage for shift workers
A shift differential is paid on top of your base rate and, under federal rules, it counts in the regular rate used to work out overtime (29 CFR 778.207(b)). A few states add daily overtime that matters on 12-hour shifts: California after 8 hours a day and double time after 12, Alaska after 8 and Colorado after 12. At $16.90 in California, a 12-hour shift pays 8 hours at the regular rate and 4 at time and a half. See the shift pay calculator for a whole year and the salary calculator to turn a rate into a yearly figure.

What is the federal minimum wage in 2026?
$7.25 an hour, set by the Fair Labor Standards Act. States and cities can set higher rates.
Which state has the highest minimum wage?
Washington, at $17.13 an hour, among the states. The District of Columbia is higher, at $18.40 (DOL table, July 1, 2026).

Do night shifts pay more than minimum wage?
Federal law does not require a night premium. If your employer pays one, it goes on top of the rate and counts in your overtime rate.

## Baylor Shift: What It Is, Hours and Pay for Nurses
URL: https://crewdays.app/baylor-shift/

Home / Guides / Baylor shift
Baylor shift: the weekend nursing schedule
A Baylor shift, or Baylor plan, is a weekend-only schedule: usually two 12-hour shifts, Saturday and Sunday, often days or nights. Hospitals that offer it pay a premium for the weekend, either a higher hourly rate or more hours of pay than you work. The exact terms change from one hospital to the next.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @equalstock on Unsplash
How a Baylor schedule works
Cycle: 7 days
Shift length: 12 hours
Hours a week: 24
Hours a year: 1,251
Most shifts in a row: 2
Longest break: 5 days
Two 12-hour shifts every weekend is 24 hours a week and about 1,251 hours a year (104 shifts in 2027). Your weekdays are always free, but you never get a weekend off unless you take leave or trade.
Hospitals use it to fill weekends, the hardest shifts to staff, so the Monday-to-Friday nurses can have most weekends off. Some versions use two 16-hour shifts or three 12-hour shifts from Friday night to Sunday night.
Baylor pay: what to ask
There is no legal definition of a Baylor shift, so ask the hospital to put these points in writing:
The pay basis. A higher weekend rate for the hours you work, or pay for more hours than you work (for example 24 hours worked paid as 36). Both are common.
Benefits. Whether the hospital treats you as full time for health insurance, paid time off and retirement, and how PTO accrues: per hour worked or per hour paid.
Missed weekends. What happens if you are sick or take leave: many contracts require you to make up a missed weekend.
Holidays. Whether you also work holidays that fall on a weekday.
Overtime on a Baylor schedule
Federal overtime is due for hours over 40 in a workweek (29 CFR 778.107), so 24 hours a weekend creates no overtime on its own. If you pick up extra shifts, overtime starts after 40 hours worked in the workweek. Hospitals may instead use the 8/80 system, agreed with staff in advance: overtime after 8 hours in a workday and after 80 hours in 14 days (29 CFR 778.601). Under 8/80, every 12-hour shift carries 4 hours of overtime, so ask which system applies to the Baylor post. Weekend premiums of at least time and a half paid for weekend work can count as overtime premium under 29 CFR 778.203.
Is a Baylor shift right for you?
It suits students, parents who share childcare with a weekday partner and nurses who want weekdays free for a second job. The cost is the weekends: about 104 weekend days a year at work. To plan around it, add your weekend shifts to the shift calendar with “Build your own” and the cycle OOOOODD (start it on a Monday). For other nursing patterns see nurse shift schedules.

Questions
What does a Baylor shift mean?
A weekend-only schedule, usually two 12-hour shifts on Saturday and Sunday, paid at a premium. It is also called the Baylor plan.
Is a Baylor shift considered full time?
It depends on the hospital. Many treat Baylor nurses as full time for benefits even though they work 24 hours a week; get it in writing.
How many hours a year is a Baylor shift?
About 1,251 hours: 24 hours a week. In 2027 a Saturday-and-Sunday schedule has 104 shifts.
Is a Baylor shift worth it?
It pays a weekend premium and leaves weekdays free, but you work almost every weekend. Compare the hourly equivalent, benefits and what happens if you miss a weekend.
Do Baylor nurses get overtime?
Not for the 24 weekend hours under the 40-hour rule. If the hospital uses the 8/80 system, hours over 8 in a day are overtime.

## Clopening Shift: What It Is and Is It Illegal?
URL: https://crewdays.app/clopening/

Home / Guides / Clopening
Clopening: closing and opening the next day
A clopening is a closing shift followed by an opening shift the next morning, often with 8 hours or less in between. Federal law does not ban it, but a few states and cities restrict it. In Oregon, large retail, hospitality and food service employers must give 10 hours of rest or pay time and a half.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @nate_dumlao on Unsplash
How short is a clopening?
| | Close | Open | Hours between
| 10:00 p.m. | 6:00 a.m. | 8
| 11:00 p.m. | 6:00 a.m. | 7
| 11:00 p.m. | 5:00 a.m. | 6
| midnight | 7:00 a.m. | 7
Take off the commute both ways and the time to wind down, and a 7-hour gap often leaves 5 hours of sleep or less. The CDC recommends at least 7 hours of sleep a day for adults (CDC).
Is clopening illegal?
Not under federal law. The Fair Labor Standards Act sets no minimum rest between shifts for adults. Some states and cities have “fair workweek” or predictive scheduling laws. Oregon's is in the state code. A covered employer may not schedule or require work in the first 10 hours after the previous day's shift unless the employee requests or consents. Any hour worked inside that rest period is paid at one and a half times the regular rate (ORS 653.442). It covers retail, hospitality and food service establishments with 500 or more employees worldwide (ORS 653.422).
Several cities, including Seattle, New York City and Chicago, have their own fair workweek rules with rest requirements for certain industries. They change and have their own coverage tests, so check your city's labor office before relying on them.
What you can do
Ask whether your employer or state has a rest rule and whether a clopening needs your consent.
Keep your own record of closing and opening times: the hours calculator works out the gap across midnight.
If you are on a rotating schedule, compare the rest between your shifts in the shift calendar.
Rest between shifts on rotating schedules
In 24/7 plants and hospitals the pattern itself sets the rest: on a 12-hour rotation you normally get at least 24 hours before a change from nights to days. In the UK, workers are entitled to 11 consecutive hours of rest in each 24-hour period; see UK working time rules and how many night shifts in a row you can work in the UK.

Days in a row you can work

Night shifts in a row (UK)

Questions
What is a clopening shift?
Closing a store or restaurant at night and opening it the next morning, with a short gap, often 8 hours or less, between the two shifts.
Is clopening illegal?
Not under federal law. Oregon requires covered large retail, hospitality and food service employers to give 10 hours of rest or pay time and a half (ORS 653.442), and some cities have similar rules.
How many hours do you need between shifts?
No federal minimum exists for adults. Oregon's rule is 10 hours for covered employers, and the UK sets 11 hours of daily rest.
Can I refuse a clopening?
Where a rest law applies, as in Oregon, you can only be scheduled inside the rest period if you request or consent. Elsewhere it depends on your employer's policy or contract.
Do you get paid more for a clopening?
In Oregon, covered employers pay time and a half for hours worked during the 10-hour rest period. Federal law has no such premium.

## 5-5-4 Schedule: 15-Day Rotation, Hours and Calendar
URL: https://crewdays.app/5-5-4-schedule/

Home / Guides / 5-5-4 schedule
5-5-4 schedule
The 5-5-4 schedule is a 15-day rotation of 12-hour shifts: 5 day shifts, 5 days off, 4 night shifts and 1 day off, then it repeats. It is usually run with three crews. The five-day break is the attraction; the catch is the average week of 50.4 hours.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @gieling on Unsplash
5-5-4 at a glance
Cycle: 15 days
Shift length: 12 hours
Hours a week: 50.4
Hours a year: 2,628
Most shifts in a row: 5
Longest break: 5 days
Crew A: Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Off, Off, Night, Night, Night, Night, Off
Crew B: Off, Off, Off, Off, Off, Night, Night, Night, Night, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day
Crew C: Night, Night, Night, Night, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Off, Off
With the three crews 5 days apart there is always one crew on days, but nights are covered on only 4 days in 5. Employers fill the gap with relief or overtime.
The math most guides skip
Each crew works 9 shifts every 15 days: 108 hours, an average of 50.4 hours a week and about 2,628 a year (220 shifts in 2027 for one crew). That is about 440 hours a year more than a four-crew 12-hour schedule such as the Pitman (2,184 hours). Under the federal rule, overtime is paid for hours over 40 in each workweek; depending on the day your workweek starts, a 5-5-4 crew works about 735 to 735 overtime hours a year.
Weekends and breaks
The cycle is 15 days, so your days move through the week. A crew gets 12 to 16, depending on the weekday your cycle starts full weekends off in 2027. The longest break is 5 days, and the change from nights back to days comes after one day off, which many people find hard. The change from days to nights comes after the five-day break.
Who uses it and alternatives
The 5-5-4 appears in plants and contact centers that run three crews. If the hours are too high, the four-crew rotations average 42 hours: compare the DuPont (also with a long break) and the other 12-hour schedules. Choose “5-5-4” in the shift calendar to get your year, with every crew, holidays and a file for your phone.

3-4-4-3 schedule
12-hour schedule with 3 crews
Southern swing schedule
8-hour schedule, every other weekend off
1-3-2-3 schedule
5-2-5-3 schedule
All guides
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
What is the 5-5-4 rotation schedule?
A 15-day rotation of 12-hour shifts: 5 days on day shift, 5 days off, 4 nights on night shift and 1 day off.
How many hours a week is a 5-5-4 schedule?
About 50.4 on average: 9 shifts of 12 hours every 15 days.
How many crews does a 5-5-4 need?
Usually three, 5 days apart. That covers the day shift every day and the night shift on 4 days in 5.
How many days off do you get on a 5-5-4?
6 days off every 15 days: a 5-day break and a single day off after the nights.
Is the 5-5-4 a good schedule?
It gives a 5-day break every cycle, but averages 50.4 hours a week and changes from nights to days after one day off.

## 3-4-4-3 Schedule: 12-Hour Calendar, Hours, Overtime
URL: https://crewdays.app/3-4-4-3-schedule/

Home / Guides / 3-4-4-3 schedule
3-4-4-3 schedule
The 3-4-4-3 schedule is 3 days on, 4 off, 4 on and 3 off: a 14-day cycle of 12-hour shifts, 84 hours every two weeks (42 a week on average). It is the 4-3-3-4 started at a different point. Started on a Monday, a crew works only weekdays.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @thisisengineering on Unsplash
3-4-4-3 at a glance
Cycle: 14 days
Shift length: 12 hours
Hours a week: 42
Hours a year: 2,190
Most shifts in a row: 4
Longest break: 4 days
Crew A: Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off
Crew B: Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Off
A week-by-week view
| | Week | Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Sat | Sun | Hours
| 1 | D | D | D | off | off | off | off | 36
| 2 | D | D | D | D | off | off | off | 48
Started on a Monday, week 1 is Monday to Wednesday and week 2 is Monday to Thursday, so every weekend is free: 52 full weekends off in 2027. Start the cycle on another day and the work days slide into the weekend: as few as 0. That is why plants pair two crews on opposite halves of the cycle, one covering Monday to Thursday and the other Thursday to Sunday, and still need relief to cover every day.
3-4-4-3 or 4-3-3-4?
They are the same cycle read from a different day: the 4-3-3-4 starts with the four-shift block. What changes is which days of the week your crew works. Compare both in the calendar with the same start date.
Overtime
The weeks alternate between 36 and 48 hours. With a Monday workweek, the 48-hour week has 8 hours of federal overtime, about 208 hours a year; moving the workweek start changes it, up to 208 (29 CFR 778.105). Choose “3-4-4-3” in the shift calendar to get your year, with every crew, holidays and a file for your phone.

8-hour schedule, every other weekend off

5-2-5-3 schedule

Questions
What is a 3-4-4-3 schedule?
3 days on, 4 off, 4 on, 3 off: a 14-day cycle of 12-hour shifts, 7 shifts and 84 hours every two weeks.
How many hours is a 3-4-4-3 schedule?
84 hours every two weeks, an average of 42 a week and about 2,184 a year.
Does the 3-4-4-3 give weekends off?
Yes, if the cycle starts on a Monday: every weekend is free (52 in 2027). Started on other days it gives fewer.
What is the difference between 3-4-4-3 and 4-3-3-4?
None in the cycle itself: the 4-3-3-4 starts with the four-shift block. The days of the week you work depend on where your crew starts.
How much overtime is on a 3-4-4-3?
With a Monday workweek, 8 hours every other week (about 208 a year). It depends on where the employer starts the workweek.

## 12-Hour Rotating Shift Schedule With 3 Teams
URL: https://crewdays.app/12-hour-shift-schedule-3-crews/

Home / Guides / 12-hour schedule with 3 crews
12-hour rotating shift schedule with 3 teams
Three teams can cover every hour of the year with 12-hour shifts, but each person then works 56 hours a week on average. The most common rotation is 2 days, 2 nights, 2 off: a 6-day cycle with the teams two days apart.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @sammoghadam on Unsplash
2 days, 2 nights, 2 off
Cycle: 6 days
Shift length: 12 hours
Hours a week: 56
Hours a year: 2,920
Most shifts in a row: 4
Longest break: 2 days
Crew A: Day, Day, Night, Night, Off, Off
Crew B: Night, Night, Off, Off, Day, Day
Crew C: Off, Off, Day, Day, Night, Night
Each day one team is on days, one on nights and one is off. In 2027 a team works 243 shifts, 121 of them nights, about 2,920 hours.
The math: why three teams means 56 hours
A week has 168 hours. Divided by three teams, each works 56 hours a week; with four teams it is 42 hours, the average of the Pitman, Panama or DuPont. So a three-team 12-hour schedule always carries about 16 hours of weekly overtime per person under the federal 40-hour rule: about 832 overtime hours a year with this rotation, whatever day the workweek starts. See the 24/7 schedules compared for crews and hours side by side.
Other three-team options
| | Rotation | Cycle | Hours a week | Most shifts in a row | Longest break | Full weekends off in 2027
| 2 days, 2 nights, 2 off | 6 days | 56 | 4 | 2 days | 8 to 9, depending on the weekday your cycle starts
| 1 day, 1 night, 1 off | 3 days | 56 | 2 | 1 day | 0
| 24/48 (one 24-hour shift) | 3 days | 56 | 1 | 2 days | 18
The fire service solves the same problem with one 24-hour shift and two days off (the 24/48), helped by the 7(k) exemption that raises their overtime threshold. In plants and hospitals, most employers add a fourth team instead.
When three teams make sense
For a short period, a seasonal peak or a small site, three teams can work with the overtime budgeted. For the long run, four teams at 42 hours are the norm. Choose “2 days, 2 nights, 2 off (3 crews)” in the shift calendar to get your year, with every crew, holidays and a file for your phone.

Questions
How do you schedule 3 teams on 12-hour shifts?
The usual way is 2 days, 2 nights, 2 off, a 6-day cycle with the teams two days apart. Each day one team is on days, one on nights and one off.
How many hours a week with 3 teams on 12-hour shifts?
56 hours on average: 168 hours a week divided by three teams.
What is a rotating 3-shift schedule?
A rotation where each team works days, nights and days off in turn, so three teams cover 24/7.
Is 3 teams enough for 24/7 coverage?
Yes, but each person works 56 hours a week, about 16 hours of overtime. Most 24/7 operations use four teams at 42 hours.
What is the best 12-hour rotating shift schedule?
With four teams, the Pitman, Panama and DuPont are the most common. With three, 2 days, 2 nights, 2 off.

## How Many Days in a Row Can You Work Legally? (US)
URL: https://crewdays.app/how-many-days-in-a-row-can-you-work/

Home / Guides / Days in a row you can work
How many days in a row can you legally work?
For adults, federal law sets no limit on how many days in a row or how many hours a day you can work: it only requires overtime pay after 40 hours in a workweek. A few states do set limits. California does not let employers cause employees to work more than six days in seven, with exceptions.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @silverkblack on Unsplash
Federal law
The Fair Labor Standards Act has no cap on hours or consecutive days for workers aged 16 and over. What it does require is time and a half for hours over 40 in a workweek (29 CFR 778.107). Limits exist for specific groups:
14- and 15-year-olds: no more than 3 hours on a school day, 8 on a non-school day, 18 a week in school weeks and 40 in other weeks, between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. (9 p.m. from June 1 to Labor Day) (29 CFR 570.35).
Truck drivers: property-carrying drivers can drive up to 11 hours within a 14-hour window after 10 consecutive hours off duty (49 CFR 395.3).
Other regulated jobs such as pilots, air traffic controllers and nuclear plant staff have rules from their own federal agencies.
State rules
| | State | Rule | Source
| California | No employer shall cause employees to work more than six days in seven. It does not apply when total hours do not exceed 30 in a week or 6 in any day. | Labor Code 552 and 556
| Maine | An employer may not require more than 80 hours of overtime in any two consecutive weeks, with exceptions for emergencies, essential services and others. | 26 M.R.S. §603
| Oregon | Covered large retail, hospitality and food service employers must give 10 hours of rest between shifts or pay time and a half. | ORS 653.442
| Several states | Limits on mandatory overtime for nurses in hospitals. | Nurse overtime laws
California also pays overtime on the seventh consecutive day in a workweek: time and a half for the first 8 hours and double time after that (Labor Code 510). Other states have day-of-rest rules for particular industries; check your state labor department.
Shift schedules and long runs
Common rotations keep runs short: the Pitman never goes above 3 shifts in a row and the DuPont 4. Longer runs belong to specific patterns, such as the 7 on 7 off or 14-day hitches on oil rigs (hitch rotations). If you are asked to work many days in a row, count the overtime: the time card calculator shows it week by week.

Baylor shift

Questions
How many days in a row can you work legally?
Federal law sets no limit for adults. California bars employers from causing employees to work more than six days in seven, unless they work 30 hours a week or less, or 6 hours a day or less.
Can I work 7 days a week?
Under federal law, yes, with overtime after 40 hours in the workweek. In California the seventh consecutive day in a workweek is paid at overtime rates.
Is a 24-hour shift legal in the USA?
Yes for adults under federal law. Fire departments commonly use 24-hour shifts. Some jobs, such as truck driving, have their own limits.
How many hours can you legally work in a day?
There is no federal daily limit for adults. Minors aged 14 and 15 are limited to 3 hours on school days and 8 on other days.
Can my employer make me work overtime?
In most states, yes. Maine limits mandatory overtime to 80 hours in two weeks, and several states limit mandatory overtime for hospital nurses.

## On-Call Pay Rules: Is On-Call Time Paid? (FLSA)
URL: https://crewdays.app/on-call-pay/

Home / Guides / On-call pay
On-call pay: when on-call time is work
Under federal rules, on-call time is paid work if you must stay on the employer's premises, or so close that you cannot use the time for yourself. If you only have to leave word where you can be reached, the waiting time is not work, but every call you answer and the time you spend on it is.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @erielreyes on Unsplash
The federal rule
“An employee who is required to remain on call on the employer's premises or so close thereto that he cannot use the time effectively for his own purposes is working while on call” (29 CFR 785.17). An employee who only needs to leave word at home or with the company where they can be reached is not working while on call. In practice the question is how restricted you are: how fast you must respond, how often you are called, and whether you can sleep, go out or see family.
Examples
| | Situation | Paid?
| Waiting at the station or on the ward for the next call | Yes: on duty (29 CFR 785.15)
| At home with a phone, free to go out, called now and then | Usually no, except the calls themselves
| Must answer in 5 minutes and be on site in 15, called most nights | Likely yes: too restricted to use the time
| Answering a call or working remotely from home | Yes, for the time worked
If you are told you can leave and do not have to start work until a set time, the period is off duty (29 CFR 785.16).
On-call pay is often more than the law
Many employers and union contracts pay a flat on-call rate per hour or shift, a minimum call-back of two to four hours, or both. Those are terms of the contract, not federal requirements. Paid on-call time that counts as work also counts toward overtime.
Fire, EMS and police on 24-hour shifts
For employees under section 7(k), the general rules of part 785 apply, with special rules for sleep time (29 CFR 553.221 and 553.222). On shifts of more than 24 hours, up to 8 hours of sleep can be left out of paid hours by agreement. Calls that interrupt it count, and if you cannot sleep at least 5 hours, the whole period counts. See the 7(k) overtime calculator and EMS shift schedules.

Clopening
Days in a row you can work
Nurse mandatory overtime laws
PTO on 12-hour shifts
Baylor shift
Minimum wage by state

Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
Does a job have to pay you to be on call?
Under federal rules, only if you must stay on the premises or are so restricted that you cannot use the time for your own purposes. Time spent on calls is always paid.
Can I say no to being on call?
Federal law does not stop employers from requiring on-call duty. Contracts, union agreements and some state rules for nurses limit it.
Are on-call calls at night paid?
Yes. The time you spend answering calls or working is hours worked, and it counts toward overtime.
What is the difference between on-call and standby?
Employers use the words differently. What decides pay is the restriction: on the premises or unable to use the time freely means work.
Is on-call time counted for overtime?
On-call time that is hours worked counts toward the 40-hour overtime threshold like any other work.

## Mandatory Overtime Laws for Nurses by State
URL: https://crewdays.app/nurse-mandatory-overtime-laws/

Home / Guides / Nurse mandatory overtime laws
Mandatory overtime laws for nurses
No federal law stops hospitals from requiring nurses to work overtime. Several states do. In Washington, no employee of a health care facility may be required to work overtime, with exceptions for emergencies and some on-call time. In Minnesota and West Virginia a nurse can decline extra hours that would put patients at risk.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @hush52 on Unsplash
States with nurse overtime laws (texts we read)
| | State | What the law says | Source
| Washington | No employee of a health care facility may be required to work overtime; refusing overtime is not grounds for discipline. Exceptions include unforeseeable emergencies and prescheduled on-call time, with limits on how on-call time can be used. | RCW 49.28.140
| Minnesota | A hospital may not take action against a nurse solely because the nurse declines additional consecutive hours beyond a normal work period, if the nurse believes it may jeopardize patient safety. A normal work period is defined in the statute. | Minn. Stat. 181.275
| West Virginia | A hospital may not mandate a nurse to accept overtime, or act against a nurse who refuses because it may jeopardize patient or employee safety. Exceptions for unforeseen emergencies, prescheduled on-call time and finishing a procedure in progress. | W. Va. Code 21-5F-3
| Maine (all employees) | An employer may not require more than 80 hours of overtime in any two consecutive weeks, with exceptions. | 26 M.R.S. §603
Other states, including Oregon, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Connecticut and Massachusetts, also restrict mandatory overtime for nurses. Their official texts were not available to us when this page was written, so they are not described here; check your state's board of nursing or labor department.
What the laws usually allow
Almost every law makes exceptions for emergencies (a disaster, a declared emergency, an unforeseen staffing crisis), for prescheduled on-call time and for finishing a procedure already under way. Several also say on-call time cannot be used as a substitute for scheduling enough staff.
What to check in your hospital's policy
Whether the hospital is covered by your state's law: some laws cover only hospitals, others other health care facilities, and some exclude nursing facilities.
What counts as an emergency or an unforeseen situation that allows mandatory overtime.
How prescheduled on-call time works, and whether it can be used to cover regular staffing.
Whether a collective bargaining agreement replaces the statute, as the West Virginia law allows.
Which overtime pay system applies: the 40-hour workweek or 8/80.
Overtime pay on 12-hour shifts: 40-hour week or 8/80
Three 12-hour shifts in a week are 36 hours, so under the 40-hour rule there is no overtime. Under the 8/80 system the same week has 12 hours of overtime, 4 for each shift, and six shifts in 14 days (72 hours) carry 24. Ask payroll which one your hospital uses before you compare job offers.
Federal law: overtime pay, not limits
The Fair Labor Standards Act sets no limit on hours. It requires overtime pay for hours over 40 in a workweek or, under the 8/80 system for hospitals, over 8 hours in a day and 80 in 14 days (29 CFR 778.601). On 12-hour shifts under 8/80, every shift carries 4 hours of overtime. Use the time card calculator to check your week and nurse shift schedules to compare rotations.

Questions
Which states ban mandatory overtime for nurses?
Washington, Minnesota and West Virginia have laws we have read in full; several others, including Oregon, New York and New Jersey, also restrict it. Most allow exceptions for emergencies and on-call time.
What is mandatory overtime for nurses?
Being required to work beyond your scheduled shift, for example staying for another shift when relief does not arrive.
Can I be fired for refusing overtime?
In states with nurse overtime laws, such as Washington and West Virginia, refusing covered overtime is not grounds for discipline. Elsewhere it depends on your contract.
Is mandatory overtime legal under federal law?
Yes. The FLSA does not limit hours; it requires overtime pay after 40 hours a week or under the 8/80 system for hospitals.
Does on-call count as mandatory overtime?
Many state laws exclude prescheduled on-call time from the ban, but limit using it as a substitute for scheduled staff.

## PTO for 12-Hour Shift Workers: How Many Days Off?
URL: https://crewdays.app/pto-12-hour-shifts/

Home / Guides / PTO on 12-hour shifts
PTO on 12-hour shifts
Paid time off is usually counted in hours, so each 12-hour shift you take off uses 12 hours. 80 hours of PTO, two weeks for a weekday worker, is only 6.7 twelve-hour shifts. Because you work fewer days, though, those shifts cover more calendar days off.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @marissacristina on Unsplash
PTO hours to shifts
| | PTO hours | 8-hour days | 12-hour shifts | 24-hour shifts
| 40 | 5 | 3.3 | 1.7
| 80 | 10 | 6.7 | 3.3
| 120 | 15 | 10 | 5
| 160 | 20 | 13.3 | 6.7
| 200 | 25 | 16.7 | 8.3
Why it still goes further than it looks
On a 12-hour rotation you work about half the days of the year, so the days off around your leave are already long. On a Pitman, taking the 3 shifts of one Friday-to-Sunday block gives you 7 days off in a row. On a DuPont, 4 shifts of leave next to the 7-day break give 14 days. On a 3 on 3 off, 3 shifts give 9. Use the shift calendar to see where your blocks fall before you book.
How PTO accrual works
Most employers accrue PTO per hour worked. A plan that gives 80 hours a year for 2,080 hours worked accrues about 0.0385 hours per hour (80 ÷ 2,080). On a 12-hour rotation with 2,184 scheduled hours, the same rate gives about 84 hours. Some plans cap the balance or accrue per pay period instead; your handbook says which.
Federal law does not require paid vacation or sick leave: the FLSA “does not require payment for time not worked, such as vacations, sick leave or federal or other holidays” (US Department of Labor). Some states and cities require paid sick leave, and PTO plans are set by the employer or union contract.
Tips for 12-hour workers
Ask whether a holiday you work is paid extra or adds PTO; see the 2027 federal holidays.
Check whether PTO counts as hours worked for overtime: under federal rules, paid leave hours do not count toward the 40.
For the year's hours and pay of your pattern, use the shift pay calculator.

Baylor shift
Minimum wage by state
Night shifts in a row (UK)
Work hours in a year
On-call pay
Clopening
All guides
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
How many days off for 12-hour shifts?
Divide your PTO hours by 12. 80 hours is 6.7 shifts, 120 hours is 10 shifts. Because shifts are grouped, a few shifts of leave can give a week or more off in a row.
How much PTO do you accrue for 40 hours?
On a plan of 80 hours a year for 2,080 hours, about 1.54 hours for every 40 hours worked (0.0385 per hour).
How much PTO do you get for a 10-hour shift?
Each 10-hour day off uses 10 hours of PTO. 80 hours covers 8 ten-hour days.
Does PTO count toward overtime?
Not under federal rules: overtime is based on hours actually worked. Some contracts count it anyway.
Is PTO required by law?
Federal law does not require paid vacation. Some states and cities require paid sick leave.

---

## 24-Hour Shift Schedule Template (A/B/C Shift), Free
URL: https://crewdays.app/24-hour-shift-schedule-template/

Home / Guides / 24-hour shift schedule template
24-hour shift schedule template
Every 24-hour schedule is a short cycle repeated all year. Pick yours below, copy the cycle or open it in the calendar, and you get a template for every platoon that you can print, download for Excel or add to a phone.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @matreding on Unsplash
The templates
| | Schedule | Cycle (X = 24 h on, O = off) | Length | Platoons | Hours a week | Hours in 28 days | Full weekends off in 2027
| 24/48 | XOO | 3 days | 3 | 56 | 216–240 h | 17 to 18, depending on the weekday your cycle starts
| 48/96 | XXOOOO | 6 days | 3 | 56 | 192–240 h | 25 to 27, depending on the weekday your cycle starts
| Kelly | XOXOXOOOO | 9 days | 3 | 56 | 216–240 h | 16 to 18, depending on the weekday your cycle starts
| 24/72 | XOOO | 4 days | 4 | 42 | 168 h | 26
| 1-3-2-3 | XOOOXXOOO | 9 days | 3 | 56 | 216–240 h | 23 to 24, depending on the weekday your cycle starts
One platoon, 2027, cycle starting Monday, January 4. Hours in 28 days is the 7(k) work period used by fire departments: overtime is due after 212 hours (29 CFR 553.230).
How to make the template for your department
Choose the schedule and the date platoon A starts a shift in the shift calendar.
Under “Show”, pick “All crews” to see A, B and C (and D on a 24/72) side by side, with your department's colors under “Crew names”.
Press “Print” for a wall calendar, “Excel” for a spreadsheet with one column per platoon, or “Embed” to put “who is on duty today” on the station website.
Add Kelly days under “Kelly days” if your department uses them.
Building a template by hand
Write the cycle once, one letter per day, then shift it for each platoon: on a 24/48 platoon B starts one day after A and platoon C two days after. In Excel, a formula such as =MID("XOO", MOD(date - start, 3) + 1, 1) returns the state of any date for a 3-day cycle. The calendar does the same for every day of the year and every platoon at once, and handles leap years and the clock changes.
Which one to choose
The 24/48 is the most common; the 48/96 halves the commutes; the 24/72 needs a fourth platoon but brings the week down to 42 hours. Compare them in 48/96 vs 24/48 and on firefighter shift schedules.

What is the most common 24-hour shift schedule?
The 24/48: one 24-hour shift, then 48 hours off, with three platoons (A, B and C).

## How Many Night Shifts in a Row Can You Work? (UK)
URL: https://crewdays.app/uk/night-shifts-in-a-row/

Home / Guides / Night shifts in a row (UK)
How many night shifts in a row can you work in the UK?
There is no legal maximum on the number of consecutive night shifts in the UK. The Working Time Regulations 1998 limit a night worker's normal hours to an average of 8 in each 24, and give every worker 11 hours' rest a day and a weekly rest period. Employers must also manage the risk of fatigue.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @c7_visuals on Unsplash
The rules that apply
| | Rule | What it says | Source
| Night work limit | A night worker's normal hours must not exceed an average of 8 hours in each 24, usually over 17 weeks. | WTR reg. 6
| Daily rest | At least 11 consecutive hours' rest in each 24-hour period (12 for young workers). | WTR reg. 10
| Weekly rest | 24 uninterrupted hours in each 7 days, or 48 hours in each 14 days if the employer decides. | WTR reg. 11
So a run of four or five 12-hour nights can be lawful: the 12 hours off between shifts meets the daily rest rule, and the average of 8 hours in 24 is worked out over weeks, not on each night. Some workers are covered by exceptions, and the rest rules can be changed by collective or workforce agreements with compensatory rest. See working time rules for shift workers for the detail.
Fatigue is the employer's duty
The Health and Safety Executive points out that accidents and injuries are more frequent on night shifts, after a succession of shifts and when shifts are long. The legal duty to manage fatigue is on the employer, whatever an individual is willing to work (HSE). If you are regularly asked to work long runs of nights, raise it with your manager or safety representative.
How common rotas compare
On a continental rota you never work more than 2 nights in a row; on a 4 on 4 off rotating pattern, 4 nights; on a DuPont-type pattern, 4. Check your own rota against the 48-hour average week and the 11-hour daily rest on the UK rota calendar, and plan the bank holidays with bank holidays for shift workers.
More guides
Work hours in a year
On-call pay
Clopening
Days in a row you can work
Nurse mandatory overtime laws
PTO on 12-hour shifts
All guides
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on 19 October 2026. How we calculate
Questions
How many night shifts in a row can you work in the UK?
There is no legal maximum. Night workers' normal hours must average no more than 8 in 24, and every worker is entitled to 11 hours' rest a day and a weekly rest period.
Are 12-hour night shifts legal in the UK?
Yes. The 8-hour limit for night workers is an average over a reference period, usually 17 weeks, not a limit on each shift (WTR reg. 6).
Can I legally work 14 days in a row in the UK?
The weekly rest rule allows an employer to give 48 hours' rest in each 14 days instead of 24 hours in each 7, so 12 days in a row can fit. Collective or workforce agreements can change this.
How much rest do I need between night shifts?
At least 11 consecutive hours in each 24-hour period (WTR reg. 10).
Who is a night worker?
Someone who normally works at least 3 hours during night time, which is 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. unless an agreement sets another 7-hour period including midnight to 5 a.m.

## Southern Swing Schedule: 8-Hour Rotation Calendar
URL: https://crewdays.app/southern-swing-schedule/

Home / Guides / Southern swing schedule
Southern swing schedule
The southern swing is a 28-day rotation of 8-hour shifts for four crews: 7 day shifts, 2 off, 7 evenings, 2 off, 7 nights and 3 off. Each day one crew is on days, one on evenings and one on nights, while the fourth is off. It rotates forward, from days to evenings to nights.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @arnosenoner on Unsplash
Southern swing at a glance
Cycle: 28 days
Shift length: 8 hours
Hours a week: 42
Hours a year: 2,190
Most shifts in a row: 7
Longest break: 3 days
Crew A: Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Off, Off, Night, Night, Night, Night, Night, Night, Night, Off, Off, Off
Crew B: Off, Off, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Off, Off, Night, Night, Night, Night, Night, Night, Night, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day
Crew C: Evening, Evening, Off, Off, Night, Night, Night, Night, Night, Night, Night, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening
Crew D: Night, Night, Night, Night, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Evening, Off, Off, Night, Night, Night
Hours and weekends
Each crew works 21 shifts every 28 days: 168 hours, 42 a week on average and about 2,190 a year. In 2027 one crew works 273 shifts: 91 days, 91 evenings and 91 nights. Full weekends off are rare, 0 to 13, depending on the weekday your cycle starts, because the breaks are only two or three days.
Seven 8-hour shifts in a row is 56 hours if they fall in one workweek. Depending on the day the employer starts the workweek, the cycle gives about 104 to 208 federal overtime hours a year (29 CFR 778.105).
Pros and cons
Pros
8-hour shifts are shorter than 12s.
Forward rotation: days, then evenings, then nights.
Everyone shares the night shifts.
Cons
Seven shifts in a row.
Only two or three days off between blocks.
You work about 273 days a year, against about 182 on 12-hour schedules.
Alternatives
Plants moving away from the southern swing often switch to 12-hour schedules with four crews, such as the Pitman or DuPont, which keep the 42-hour average with fewer working days. See 1st, 2nd and 3rd shift hours and swing shift. Choose “Southern swing” in the shift calendar to get your year, with every crew, holidays and a file for your phone.

1-3-2-3 schedule
5-2-5-3 schedule
24-hour shift schedule template
Swing shift
1st, 2nd and 3rd shift hours
All guides

Questions
What is a southern swing schedule?
A 28-day rotation of 8-hour shifts for four crews: 7 days, 2 off, 7 evenings, 2 off, 7 nights, 3 off.
How many hours is a southern swing?
168 hours every 28 days, an average of 42 a week and about 2,190 a year.
What is an 8-hour southern swing shift?
Each 8-hour shift is a day, evening or night shift, such as 7 to 3, 3 to 11 and 11 to 7, and each crew works seven of each in turn.
How many days off do you get on a southern swing?
7 days off every 28: two breaks of 2 days and one of 3.
Is the southern swing a good schedule?
It keeps shifts to 8 hours and rotates forward, but has 7-shift runs and short breaks, with few full weekends off.

## 8-Hour Shift Schedule With Every Other Weekend Off
URL: https://crewdays.app/8-hour-shift-schedule-every-other-weekend-off/

Home / Guides / 8-hour schedule, every other weekend off
8-hour shift schedule with every other weekend off
With 8-hour shifts and 40 hours a week, you can have every other weekend off by working 10 shifts in each two-week period: one week Monday to Friday, the next week Saturday and Sunday plus three weekdays. Two people on opposite weeks cover every day of the week.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @cuongduyenceramics on Unsplash
The two-week pattern
| | Week | Sat | Sun | Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Hours
| A | off | off | D | D | D | D | D | 40
| B | D | D | off | D | D | D | off | 40
Read as one cycle from Saturday of week A: OODDDDDDDODDDO. That is 10 shifts in 14 days, 80 hours, 40 every week, so there is no weekly overtime if the workweek starts on Saturday. The cost is a run of up to 7 shifts in a row across the weekend you work. In 2027 it gives 0 to 26, depending on the weekday your cycle starts full weekends off.
Two people, every day covered
Give the second person the same pattern a week later. Then at least one of them is on duty every day, and on Tuesday to Thursday both are, which leaves room for training, meetings or the busiest days. If you need exactly one person each day, a third person on a different split, or 12-hour shifts, works better. For full 24/7 coverage with 8-hour shifts, see the southern swing and 24/7 schedules compared.
Shorter runs: the 12-hour version
If 7 shifts in a row is too many, the 12-hour Pitman (2-2-3) also gives every other weekend off, never more than 3 shifts in a row and a three-day weekend each fortnight, at 42 hours a week. 12-hour schedules with every other weekend off compares the options.
Make the calendar
In the shift calendar choose “Build your own”, type OODDDDDDDODDDO with 8-hour shifts and set the start to a Saturday you have off. Share the link with whoever covers the other weeks.

5-2-5-3 schedule
24-hour shift schedule template

1st, 2nd and 3rd shift hours
4-5-5 shift pattern
All guides

Questions
How do I make an 8-hour schedule with every other weekend off?
Work Monday to Friday one week, then Saturday, Sunday and three weekdays the next: 10 shifts and 80 hours every two weeks, with every other weekend off.
How many hours a week is it?
40 hours every week, if the workweek starts on Saturday.
What is a rotating weekend schedule with 8-hour shifts?
A pattern where staff alternate working weekends, so each person has every other weekend off while the weekends stay covered.
What is the schedule called when you have every other Friday off?
That is a 9/80 schedule: eight 9-hour days and one 8-hour day every two weeks. See the 9/80 schedule calendar.
How many days in a row will I work?
Up to 7 with this pattern, around the weekend you work. The 12-hour Pitman keeps runs to 3.

## 1-3-2-3 Firefighter Schedule: Calendar and Hours
URL: https://crewdays.app/1-3-2-3-schedule/

Home / Guides / 1-3-2-3 schedule
1-3-2-3 firefighter schedule
The 1-3-2-3 schedule is one 24-hour shift, three days off, two 24-hour shifts back to back and three days off, then it repeats. With three platoons it covers every day of the year, and every stretch off is at least three days long.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @mchesin on Unsplash
1-3-2-3 at a glance
Cycle: 9 days
Shift length: 24 hours
Hours a week: 56
Hours a year: 2,920
Most shifts in a row: 2
Longest break: 3 days
Crew A: 24h, Off, Off, Off, 24h, 24h, Off, Off, Off
Crew B: Off, 24h, 24h, Off, Off, Off, 24h, Off, Off
Crew C: Off, Off, Off, 24h, Off, Off, Off, 24h, 24h
Three shifts in nine days is 72 hours, an average of 56 hours a week and about 2,920 a year (121 shifts in 2027 for one platoon). That is the same as a 24/48 or a 48/96: the 1-3-2-3 only arranges the days differently.
How it compares
| | Schedule | Cycle | Longest stretch on | Breaks | Hours a week
| 1-3-2-3 | 9 days | 48 hours | 3 days, twice per cycle | 56
| 24/48 | 3 days | 24 hours | 2 days after every shift | 56
| 48/96 | 6 days | 48 hours | 4 days | 56
| Kelly | 9 days | 24 hours | 4 days once per cycle | 56
It sits between the 24/48 and the 48/96: one single shift and one double each cycle, and always three days off in between. Departments that test it usually want longer breaks than the 24/48 without making every tour 48 hours.
Overtime under 7(k)
Fire departments usually pay overtime after 212 hours in a 28-day work period (29 CFR 553.230). A 1-3-2-3 puts 216 or 240 hours into any 28 days, so most work periods carry some overtime, as on a 24/48. Weekends: 23 to 24, depending on the weekday your cycle starts full weekends off in 2027. Try your own work period in the 7(k) calculator.
Make the calendar
Choose “1-3-2-3” in the shift calendar to get your year, with every crew, holidays and a file for your phone. Pick “All crews” for the A, B and C platoon calendar, or see the 24-hour schedule templates.

Questions
What is a 1/3 2/3 shift schedule?
One 24-hour shift, three days off, two 24-hour shifts back to back, three days off: a 9-day cycle for fire departments.
How many hours a week is a 1-3-2-3 schedule?
56 on average with three platoons: 72 hours every 9 days.
Is 1-3-2-3 better than 48/96?
Same hours. The 1-3-2-3 mixes one 24 and one 48 per cycle with 3-day breaks; the 48/96 always works 48 hours and gives 4 days off.
How many platoons does a 1-3-2-3 need?
Three, three days apart, for one platoon on duty every day.
Does a 1-3-2-3 have overtime?
Under 7(k), most 28-day work periods go over the 212-hour threshold, as on a 24/48.

## 5-2-5-3 Work Schedule: 15-Day Cycle Explained
URL: https://crewdays.app/5-2-5-3-schedule/

Home / Guides / 5-2-5-3 schedule
5-2-5-3 work schedule
The 5-2-5-3 schedule is 5 days on, 2 off, 5 on and 3 off, a 15-day cycle usually worked with 8-hour shifts. Each person works 10 shifts every 15 days, and with three squads five days apart, two squads are on duty every day.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @michael_f on Unsplash
5-2-5-3 at a glance
Cycle: 15 days
Shift length: 8 hours
Hours a week: 37.3
Hours a year: 1,947
Most shifts in a row: 5
Longest break: 3 days
Crew A: Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off
Crew B: Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day
Crew C: Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day
Hours and coverage
10 shifts of 8 hours in 15 days is 80 hours, an average of 37.3 hours a week and about 1,947 a year (242 shifts in 2027). That is less than 40 a week, so employers often add training days or use the spare capacity for court time and leave cover. With three squads, two are on duty every day, which suits a department that wants extra staff on each shift or runs the squads on different shift times.
Because the cycle is 15 days, the days off move through the week: 9 to 12, depending on the weekday your cycle starts full weekends off in 2027. The 3-day break comes once per cycle, about every two weeks. Some weeks have 6 shifts (48 hours), so check how overtime is counted: the federal rule pays after 40 hours in the workweek, and police agencies under 7(k) after 171 hours in 28 days (29 CFR 553.230).
Similar schedules
For 10- and 12-hour police patterns, see police shift schedules. Other 8-hour options are the southern swing and the 8-hour schedule with every other weekend off. Choose “5-2-5-3” in the shift calendar to get your year, with every crew, holidays and a file for your phone.

5-5-4 schedule

Questions
How does a 5/2/5/3 schedule work?
You work 5 days, have 2 off, work 5 more and have 3 off. The 15-day cycle then repeats.
How many hours a week is a 5-2-5-3 schedule?
About 37.3 on average with 8-hour shifts: 80 hours every 15 days.
How many squads does a 5-2-5-3 need?
Three, five days apart. Two squads are then on duty every day.
Do you get weekends off on a 5-2-5-3?
Sometimes: the cycle is 15 days, so days off move through the week. One person gets 9 to 12, depending on the weekday your cycle starts full weekends off in 2027.
Who uses the 5-2-5-3 schedule?
It appears in police departments and other services that run three squads on 8-hour shifts.

## 4-5-5 Shift Pattern (4 On 5 Off 5 On): Calendar, Hours
URL: https://crewdays.app/4-5-5-shift-pattern/

Home / Guides / 4-5-5 shift pattern
4-5-5 shift pattern (4/5/5/4/5/5)
The 4-5-5 shift pattern, also written 4/5/5/4/5/5, is 4 shifts on, 5 days off, 5 on, 4 off, 5 on and 5 off: a 28-day cycle of 12-hour shifts. Each crew works 14 shifts every 28 days, 42 hours a week on average, and two crews 14 days apart cover every day exactly once.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @plataformacolsan on Unsplash
4-5-5 at a glance
Cycle: 28 days
Shift length: 12 hours
Hours a week: 42
Hours a year: 2,190
Most shifts in a row: 5
Longest break: 5 days
Crew A: Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Off, Off
Crew B: Off, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Off, Off, Off, Off, Off, Day, Day, Day, Day, Day
Why two crews fit exactly
The second half of the cycle is the mirror of the first: crew B, starting 14 days after crew A, works on exactly the days crew A is off. So two crews give one crew on duty every day, with no gaps and no doubled days, and four crews (two on days, two on nights) cover 24/7. We checked this day by day with the calendar engine for all 28 days of the cycle. Pitman and 7 on 7 off schedules share the same property; the 4-5-5 gets there with longer breaks.
Days off and leave
The breaks are 5, 4 and 5 days, so you are never off for less than four days at a time and never work more than 5 shifts in a row. The 4-shift block sits between the two 5-day breaks: book those 4 shifts as leave and you get 14 days off in a row for 48 hours of leave. Full weekends off in 2027: 13 to 26, depending on the weekday your cycle starts.
Hours and overtime
The weeks are uneven. Under the federal rule overtime is paid for hours over 40 in each workweek, and the employer chooses the day it starts (29 CFR 778.105). For one crew:
| | Workweek starts | Hours in each of the 4 weeks | Overtime hours a year
| Monday | 48, 60, 36, 24 | 364
| Tuesday | 36, 60, 48, 24 | 364
| Wednesday | 24, 60, 60, 24 | 520
| Thursday | 24, 48, 60, 36 | 364
| Friday | 24, 36, 60, 48 | 364
| Saturday | 36, 36, 48, 48 | 208
| Sunday | 48, 36, 36, 48 | 208
So the same schedule can mean anywhere from 208 to 520 overtime hours a year. One Canadian union agreement adopted the 4/5/5/4/5/5 rotation in 2022. It starts shifts at 6:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. and pays overtime after 12 hours in a day instead (UFCW Local 401 letter of understanding): check your own contract.
4-5-5 compared
| | Pattern | Cycle | Most shifts in a row | Longest break | Full weekends off in 2027
| 4-5-5 | 28 days | 5 | 5 days | 13 to 26, depending on the weekday your cycle starts
| Pitman (2-2-3) | 14 days | 3 | 3 days | 0 to 26, depending on the weekday your cycle starts
| DuPont | 28 days | 4 | 7 days | 0 to 26, depending on the weekday your cycle starts
| 4 on 4 off | 8 days | 4 | 4 days | 18 to 21, depending on the weekday your cycle starts
All four average 42 hours a week on 12-hour shifts. The 4-5-5 trades the Pitman's short blocks for longer breaks, and the DuPont's 7-day break for a pattern that never drops below four days off. In the UK, 42 hours is within the 48-hour average week, and 12-hour shifts leave the 11 hours of daily rest the Working Time Regulations require; see UK working time rules.
Make your calendar
Choose “4-5-5 (4 on 5 off 5 on)” in the shift calendar to get your year, with every crew, holidays and a file for your phone. Pick “Night shift” under Version for the night crews, or “All crews” to see both crews side by side. Other 12-hour patterns are compared in 12-hour shift schedules.
More guides
5-5-4 schedule
3-4-4-3 schedule
12-hour schedule with 3 crews
Southern swing schedule
8-hour schedule, every other weekend off
1-3-2-3 schedule
All guides
Figures are worked out from each cycle; rules checked against official sources on October 19, 2026. How we calculate
Questions
What is a 4-5-5 shift pattern?
4 shifts on, 5 days off, 5 on, 4 off, 5 on, 5 off: a 28-day cycle, usually with 12-hour shifts. It is also written 4/5/5/4/5/5.
How many hours a week is a 4-5-5 shift pattern?
42 hours on average with 12-hour shifts: 14 shifts (168 hours) every 28 days, about 2,190 hours a year.
How many crews does a 4-5-5 need?
Two crews 14 days apart cover one shift every day exactly once; four crews cover days and nights 24/7.
What is the longest break on a 4-5-5?
5 days, twice per cycle, with a 4-day break in between. Taking the 4-shift block as leave gives 14 days off in a row.
Is the 4-5-5 shift pattern any good?
It suits people who want breaks of at least four days and no more than five shifts in a row. The cost is uneven weeks, from 24 to 60 hours, which affects weekly overtime.

## UTC Time Now: What UTC Is and How to Convert It
URL: https://crewdays.app/utc-time/

Home / Guides / UTC time
UTC time now
UTC, Coordinated Universal Time, is the time standard that the world's clocks are set from. US time zones are defined by law as a number of hours behind it: Eastern Standard Time is UTC−5, Central UTC−6, Mountain UTC−7 and Pacific UTC−8. During daylight saving time each of them moves one hour closer to UTC; UTC itself never changes.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Right now in UTC: --:--:--
US time zones and UTC
| | Zone | Standard time | Daylight saving time | Examples
| Atlantic | UTC−4 | No change | Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands
| Eastern | UTC−5 (EST) | UTC−4 (EDT) | New York, Washington, Atlanta, Miami
| Central | UTC−6 (CST) | UTC−5 (CDT) | Chicago, Dallas, Houston, Minneapolis
| Mountain | UTC−7 (MST) | UTC−6 (MDT) | Denver, Salt Lake City; Phoenix stays on MST
| Pacific | UTC−8 (PST) | UTC−7 (PDT) | Los Angeles, Seattle, Las Vegas
| Alaska | UTC−9 (AKST) | UTC−8 (AKDT) | Anchorage
| Hawaii-Aleutian | UTC−10 (HST) | No change in Hawaii | Honolulu
| Samoa | UTC−11 | No change | American Samoa
| Chamorro | UTC+10 | No change | Guam, Northern Mariana Islands
Federal law divides the United States into nine zones and defines each one by its distance from Coordinated Universal Time (15 U.S.C. 261). Daylight saving time runs from 2 a.m. on the second Sunday of March to 2 a.m. on the first Sunday of November (15 U.S.C. 260a); Hawaii and most of Arizona stay on standard time all year.
Convert UTC to your time
Photo: @davcohpho on Unsplash
UTC to US time, hour by hour (winter)
| | UTC | Eastern Time | Central Time | Mountain Time | Pacific Time
| 12:00 a.m. | 7:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 6:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 5:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 4:00 p.m. (−1 day)
| 1:00 a.m. | 8:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 7:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 6:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 5:00 p.m. (−1 day)
| 2:00 a.m. | 9:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 8:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 7:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 6:00 p.m. (−1 day)
| 3:00 a.m. | 10:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 9:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 8:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 7:00 p.m. (−1 day)
| 4:00 a.m. | 11:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 10:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 9:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 8:00 p.m. (−1 day)
| 5:00 a.m. | 12:00 a.m. | 11:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 10:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 9:00 p.m. (−1 day)
| 6:00 a.m. | 1:00 a.m. | 12:00 a.m. | 11:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 10:00 p.m. (−1 day)
| 7:00 a.m. | 2:00 a.m. | 1:00 a.m. | 12:00 a.m. | 11:00 p.m. (−1 day)
| 8:00 a.m. | 3:00 a.m. | 2:00 a.m. | 1:00 a.m. | 12:00 a.m.
| 9:00 a.m. | 4:00 a.m. | 3:00 a.m. | 2:00 a.m. | 1:00 a.m.
| 10:00 a.m. | 5:00 a.m. | 4:00 a.m. | 3:00 a.m. | 2:00 a.m.
| 11:00 a.m. | 6:00 a.m. | 5:00 a.m. | 4:00 a.m. | 3:00 a.m.
| 12:00 p.m. | 7:00 a.m. | 6:00 a.m. | 5:00 a.m. | 4:00 a.m.
| 1:00 p.m. | 8:00 a.m. | 7:00 a.m. | 6:00 a.m. | 5:00 a.m.
| 2:00 p.m. | 9:00 a.m. | 8:00 a.m. | 7:00 a.m. | 6:00 a.m.
| 3:00 p.m. | 10:00 a.m. | 9:00 a.m. | 8:00 a.m. | 7:00 a.m.
| 4:00 p.m. | 11:00 a.m. | 10:00 a.m. | 9:00 a.m. | 8:00 a.m.
| 5:00 p.m. | 12:00 p.m. | 11:00 a.m. | 10:00 a.m. | 9:00 a.m.
| 6:00 p.m. | 1:00 p.m. | 12:00 p.m. | 11:00 a.m. | 10:00 a.m.
| 7:00 p.m. | 2:00 p.m. | 1:00 p.m. | 12:00 p.m. | 11:00 a.m.
| 8:00 p.m. | 3:00 p.m. | 2:00 p.m. | 1:00 p.m. | 12:00 p.m.
| 9:00 p.m. | 4:00 p.m. | 3:00 p.m. | 2:00 p.m. | 1:00 p.m.
| 10:00 p.m. | 5:00 p.m. | 4:00 p.m. | 3:00 p.m. | 2:00 p.m.
| 11:00 p.m. | 6:00 p.m. | 5:00 p.m. | 4:00 p.m. | 3:00 p.m.
Standard time, for example January 15, 2027. From March to early November, add one hour to each US column: 14:00 UTC is 10:00 a.m. Eastern instead of 9:00 a.m.
UTC and GMT
Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) is the UK's civil time in winter and shows the same clock time as UTC. The difference is that the UK changes its clocks: British Summer Time (BST), UTC+1, runs from 1 a.m. GMT on the last Sunday in March to 1 a.m. GMT on the last Sunday in October (Summer Time Order 2002). UTC stays the same all year, which is why logs, flight plans and servers use it.
Zulu time and the 24-hour clock
Aviation, the military and many control rooms write UTC on the 24-hour clock with a “Z”, for “Zulu”: 1400Z is 14:00 UTC. To read 24-hour times, see the military time chart.
UTC on shift work
If your rota is shared between sites in different zones, or your shift logs are stamped in UTC, convert once and write both times on the handover. A night shift that runs 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. Eastern is 00:00 to 12:00 UTC in winter and 23:00 to 11:00 UTC in summer. The night the US clocks change, that shift lasts 13 or 11 hours: see daylight saving time dates.

Questions
What is the UTC time zone?
UTC is not a local time zone but the world time standard that time zones are defined from. Its offset is zero, and it does not change for daylight saving time.
Is UTC 4 or 5 hours ahead of EST?
5 hours ahead of Eastern Standard Time (winter) and 4 hours ahead of Eastern Daylight Time, used from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November.
How do I convert UTC to local time?
Subtract your zone's offset: 5 hours for EST, 6 for CST, 7 for MST and 8 for PST, one hour less during daylight saving time. 14:00 UTC is 9:00 a.m. EST.
Is UTC time the same as EST?
No. EST is UTC minus 5 hours (15 U.S.C. 261).
Is UTC the same as GMT?
They show the same time in winter. GMT is the UK's winter time; in summer the UK uses BST, one hour ahead of UTC.

## EST Time Now: Eastern Time, EST vs EDT (2026)
URL: https://crewdays.app/est-time/

Home / Guides / EST time
Eastern Time: EST and EDT
Eastern Standard Time (EST) is UTC−5. From 2 a.m. on the second Sunday in March to 2 a.m. on the first Sunday in November, the Eastern zone uses Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), UTC−4. In 2026 the zone returns to EST on Sunday, November 1. New York, Washington, Atlanta, Miami and Detroit are on Eastern Time.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Right now in New York: --:--:--
EST or EDT? The change dates
| | Year | Daylight time starts (2 a.m.) | Standard time returns (2 a.m.)
| 2026 | Sunday, March 8 | Sunday, November 1
| 2027 | Sunday, March 14 | Sunday, November 7
| 2028 | Sunday, March 12 | Sunday, November 5
The dates come from federal law (15 U.S.C. 260a). People often say “EST” all year; strictly, summer time is EDT. “ET” covers both.
Convert Eastern Time
Photo: @impatrickt on Unsplash
Eastern Time compared with other zones
| | When it is noon Eastern | Central | Mountain | Pacific | UTC | London
| Winter (EST) | 11:00 a.m. | 10:00 a.m. | 9:00 a.m. | 17:00 | 5:00 p.m.
| Summer (EDT) | 11:00 a.m. | 10:00 a.m. | 9:00 a.m. | 16:00 | 5:00 p.m.
London is usually 5 hours ahead. Because the UK and US change their clocks on different Sundays, the gap is 4 hours for about three weeks in March and one week around the end of October.
Where Eastern Time applies
The Eastern zone covers the eastern United States west of 67°30′ W and includes all of Maine (49 CFR 71.4). Its western edge is the line between the Eastern and Central zones, which crosses Michigan, Indiana, Kentucky, Tennessee and Florida, so parts of those states use Central Time (49 CFR 71.5).

| 11:00 p.m. | 10:00 p.m. | 8:00 p.m. | 4:00 a.m. (+1 day)
On a night shift
When standard time returns on November 1, 2026, the hour from 1:00 to 2:00 a.m. Eastern happens twice, so a 12-hour night shift lasts 13 hours; in March it lasts 11. The night shift clock change calculator works out the hours and pay. For pay periods and holidays, see the 2027 pay period calendar.

Questions
What time zone is EST in the USA?
Eastern Standard Time, UTC−5, used in the eastern United States in winter. In summer the same zone uses EDT, UTC−4.
Is New York on EST or EDT right now?
New York uses EDT from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November and EST the rest of the year. In 2026 it switches to EST on Sunday, November 1.
What is the difference between EST and ET?
EST is the winter standard time (UTC−5). ET, Eastern Time, means whichever is in use: EST in winter, EDT in summer.
How many hours ahead is EST from PST?
3 hours. Noon Eastern is 9:00 a.m. Pacific, all year.
How far ahead of EST is London?
Usually 5 hours. For about three weeks in March and one week at the end of October it is 4, because the UK and US change clocks on different dates.

## CST Time Now: Central Time, CST vs CDT (2026)
URL: https://crewdays.app/cst-time/

Home / Guides / CST time
Central Time: CST and CDT
Central Standard Time (CST) is UTC−6, one hour behind Eastern Time. During daylight saving time, from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November, the zone uses Central Daylight Time (CDT), UTC−5. Chicago, Dallas, Houston, Minneapolis, New Orleans and nearly all of Texas are on Central Time.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Right now in Chicago: --:--:--
CST or CDT? The change dates
| | Year | Daylight time starts (2 a.m.) | Standard time returns (2 a.m.)
| 2026 | Sunday, March 8 | Sunday, November 1
| 2027 | Sunday, March 14 | Sunday, November 7
| 2028 | Sunday, March 12 | Sunday, November 5
Set by federal law (15 U.S.C. 260a). In 2026 the Central zone returns to CST on Sunday, November 1 at 2:00 a.m.
Convert Central Time
Photo: @jbrown1276 on Unsplash
Is Texas on Central Time?
Yes, except the far west. The boundary between the Central and Mountain zones runs down the western edge of Texas, then along the east line of Hudspeth County to the Mexican border (49 CFR 71.7, paragraph (e)). So Hudspeth and El Paso counties are on Mountain Time and the rest of Texas on Central.
Where Central Time applies
The Central zone lies between the Eastern–Central line (49 CFR 71.5) and the Central–Mountain line (49 CFR 71.7). Both lines cross states: the eastern one splits Michigan, Indiana, Kentucky, Tennessee and Florida; the western one splits North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas and Texas. Illinois, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and Oklahoma are on Central Time.

| All year | 1:00 p.m. | 11:00 a.m. | 10:00 a.m. | 18:00 / 17:00

| 12:00 a.m. | 1:00 a.m. | 10:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 6:00 a.m.
| 1:00 a.m. | 2:00 a.m. | 11:00 p.m. (−1 day) | 7:00 a.m.

| 4:00 a.m. | 5:00 a.m. | 2:00 a.m. | 10:00 a.m.
| 5:00 a.m. | 6:00 a.m. | 3:00 a.m. | 11:00 a.m.
| 6:00 a.m. | 7:00 a.m. | 4:00 a.m. | 12:00 p.m.
| 7:00 a.m. | 8:00 a.m. | 5:00 a.m. | 1:00 p.m.
| 8:00 a.m. | 9:00 a.m. | 6:00 a.m. | 2:00 p.m.
| 9:00 a.m. | 10:00 a.m. | 7:00 a.m. | 3:00 p.m.
| 10:00 a.m. | 11:00 a.m. | 8:00 a.m. | 4:00 p.m.

| 1:00 p.m. | 2:00 p.m. | 11:00 a.m. | 7:00 p.m.
| 2:00 p.m. | 3:00 p.m. | 12:00 p.m. | 8:00 p.m.
| 3:00 p.m. | 4:00 p.m. | 1:00 p.m. | 9:00 p.m.
| 4:00 p.m. | 5:00 p.m. | 2:00 p.m. | 10:00 p.m.

| 8:00 p.m. | 9:00 p.m. | 6:00 p.m. | 2:00 a.m. (+1 day)
| 9:00 p.m. | 10:00 p.m. | 7:00 p.m. | 3:00 a.m. (+1 day)
| 10:00 p.m. | 11:00 p.m. | 8:00 p.m. | 4:00 a.m. (+1 day)
| 11:00 p.m. | 12:00 a.m. (+1 day) | 9:00 p.m. | 5:00 a.m. (+1 day)
Winter (standard time), for example January 15, 2027.
Shift handovers across zones
A plant in Houston and a control room in Atlanta are an hour apart: a 6 a.m. Central start is 7 a.m. Eastern. Write both times on shared rotas, and note that both zones change on the same night, so the gap stays one hour. For your own rotation, the shift calendar shows every shift of the year.

Questions
Is Texas in CST?
Most of Texas is on Central Time (CST in winter, CDT in summer). Hudspeth and El Paso counties in the far west are on Mountain Time (49 CFR 71.7).
What is the CST time zone?
Central Standard Time, UTC−6, used in the central United States in winter. In summer the zone uses CDT, UTC−5.
Is CST 1 hour or 2 hours behind EST?
1 hour. Noon Eastern is 11:00 a.m. Central, all year.
What is CST and EST?
Central and Eastern Standard Time, the winter times of the two zones: UTC−6 and UTC−5.
Is Chicago on CST?
Chicago is on Central Time: CST in winter and CDT from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November.

## PST to EST: Pacific to Eastern Time Converter
URL: https://crewdays.app/pst-to-est/

Home / Guides / PST to EST
PST to EST
Add 3 hours to Pacific Time to get Eastern Time: 9:00 a.m. PST is 12:00 p.m. EST, and 11:00 a.m. PST is 2:00 p.m. EST. The difference stays at 3 hours all year, because both zones change their clocks for daylight saving time on the same night.
By Asier Fernández · October 18, 2026
Photo: @ventiviews on Unsplash
PST to EST conversion table
| | Pacific Time | Eastern Time
| 12:00 a.m. | 3:00 a.m.
| 1:00 a.m. | 4:00 a.m.
| 2:00 a.m. | 5:00 a.m.
| 3:00 a.m. | 6:00 a.m.
| 4:00 a.m. | 7:00 a.m.
| 5:00 a.m. | 8:00 a.m.
| 6:00 a.m. | 9:00 a.m.
| 7:00 a.m. | 10:00 a.m.
| 8:00 a.m. | 11:00 a.m.
| 9:00 a.m. | 12:00 p.m.
| 10:00 a.m. | 1:00 p.m.
| 11:00 a.m. | 2:00 p.m.
| 12:00 p.m. | 3:00 p.m.
| 1:00 p.m. | 4:00 p.m.
| 2:00 p.m. | 5:00 p.m.
| 3:00 p.m. | 6:00 p.m.
| 4:00 p.m. | 7:00 p.m.
| 5:00 p.m. | 8:00 p.m.
| 6:00 p.m. | 9:00 p.m.
| 7:00 p.m. | 10:00 p.m.
| 8:00 p.m. | 11:00 p.m.
| 9:00 p.m. | 12:00 a.m. (+1 day)
| 10:00 p.m. | 1:00 a.m. (+1 day)
| 11:00 p.m. | 2:00 a.m. (+1 day)
The same in summer (PDT to EDT): the gap does not change.
EST to PST
Go the other way by subtracting 3 hours: 9:00 a.m. Eastern is 6:00 a.m. Pacific, and 5:00 p.m. Eastern is 2:00 p.m. Pacific. After 9:00 p.m. Pacific it is already the next day in the East.
PST, PDT, EST and EDT
Pacific Standard Time is UTC−8 and Eastern Standard Time UTC−5 (15 U.S.C. 261). From 2 a.m. on the second Sunday in March to 2 a.m. on the first Sunday in November both use daylight time, PDT (UTC−7) and EDT (UTC−4) (15 U.S.C. 260a). Most people write “PST” and “EST” all year; the 3-hour gap is the same either way. Most of Arizona stays on standard time, so in summer it matches Pacific Time and in winter Mountain Time.
Arizona and Hawaii
Most of Arizona and all of Hawaii stay on standard time all year, as federal law allows. So in summer, noon in Los Angeles is noon in Phoenix and 9:00 a.m. in Honolulu; in winter, noon in Los Angeles is 1:00 p.m. in Phoenix and 10:00 a.m. in Honolulu. Denver, on Mountain Time with daylight saving, is always one hour ahead of Los Angeles.
Working hours that overlap
A 9-to-5 day on each coast overlaps for 5 hours: from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Pacific, which is 12:00 to 5:00 p.m. Eastern. Calls that must include both coasts fit best between 12:00 and 2:00 p.m. Eastern (9:00 to 11:00 a.m. Pacific), clear of the East Coast's late afternoon and the West Coast's early morning.
Handovers between coasts
| | Eastern shift | Same shift in Pacific Time
| 7:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m. | 4:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.
| 7:00 p.m. – 7:00 a.m. | 4:00 p.m. – 4:00 a.m.
| 8:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. | 5:00 a.m. – 1:30 p.m.
| 11:00 p.m. – 7:00 a.m. | 8:00 p.m. – 4:00 a.m.
National dispatch centers, help desks and on-call teams that span both coasts often schedule in Eastern Time. If you start at 6:00 a.m. Pacific to join a 9:00 a.m. Eastern huddle, count those hours like any other: the hours calculator works out your day, and Eastern Time has the clock change dates.

Questions
Is PST 3 hours behind EST?
Yes. Pacific Time is 3 hours behind Eastern Time all year, including during daylight saving time.
What time is 11 a.m. PST in EST?
2:00 p.m. EST.
How do I convert PST to EST?
Add 3 hours. If the result passes midnight, it is the next day in the East: 10:00 p.m. PST is 1:00 a.m. EST.
Is 1 p.m. EST the same as 10 a.m. PST?
Yes. 1:00 p.m. Eastern is 10:00 a.m. Pacific.
What is 9 a.m. PST in EST?
12:00 p.m. (noon) EST.

5-2-5-3 work scheduleThe 5-2-5-3 schedule is 5 on, 2 off, 5 on, 3 off: a 15-day cycle of 8-hour shifts for three squads. Hours a week, weekends off and daily coverage.
4-5-5 shift pattern (4/5/5/4/5/5)The 4-5-5 shift pattern is 4 on, 5 off, 5 on, 4 off, 5 on, 5 off: a 28-day cycle of 12-hour shifts. Two crews cover every day; 42 hours a week.
UTC time nowCurrent UTC time, what Coordinated Universal Time is and how far each US time zone is behind it: EST is UTC−5, PST UTC−8, one hour less in summer.
Eastern Time: EST and EDTEastern Time is EST (UTC−5) in winter and EDT (UTC−4) from March to November. Current time, the 2026–2028 change dates, conversions and where it applies.
Central Time: CST and CDTCentral Time is CST (UTC−6) in winter and CDT (UTC−5) in summer, one hour behind Eastern. Current time, where it applies, Texas and conversions.
PST to ESTPacific Time is 3 hours behind Eastern Time all year: 9 a.m. PST is 12 p.m. EST. Hour-by-hour table, a converter and shift handover examples.
